感到焦虑是生活的正常组成部分。许多人会担心健康、金钱、学校、工作或家庭等事情。但焦虑症涉及的不仅仅是偶尔的担忧或恐惧。对于患有这些疾病的人来说，焦虑不会消失，会在许多情况下被感受到，并且可能随着时间的推移而加重。焦虑症有几种类型，包括：广泛性焦虑症惊恐障碍社交焦虑症各种恐惧症相关障碍

英文原文：
Feeling anxious is a normal part of life. Many people worry about things such as health, money, school, work, or family. But anxiety disorders involve more than occasional worry or fear. For people with these disorders, anxiety does not go away, is felt in many situations, and can get worse over time.
There are several types of anxiety disorders, including:
Generalized anxiety disorder
Panic disorder
Social anxiety disorder
Various phobia-related disorders

In severe cases, a person might feel intense fear in common situations, avoid social encounters, or refuse to leave their home.

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
每个人有时都会感到悲伤或情绪低落，但这些感觉通常会随时间过去。抑郁（也称为重性抑郁障碍或临床抑郁）则不同。它可能导致严重症状，影响你的感受、思维以及处理日常活动的方式，例如睡眠、进食或工作。它是一种可能影响任何人的疾病——无论年龄、种族、收入、文化或教育程度。研究表明，遗传、生物、环境和心理因素在抑郁中起作用。

英文原文：
Everyone feels sad or low sometimes, but these feelings usually pass with time. Depression (also called major depressive disorder or clinical depression) is different. It can cause severe symptoms that affect how you feel, think, and handle daily activities, such as sleeping, eating, or working. It is an illness that can affect anyone—regardless of age, race, income, culture, or education. Research suggests that genetic, biological, environmental, and psychological factors play a role in depression.

Depression is one of the most common mental disorders in the United States. The symptoms range from mild to severe and can disrupt a person’s ability to carry out everyday activities. It is linked to increased health care costs and other health conditions like heart disease and diabetes. It is also a risk factor for suicidal thoughts and behaviors.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
自我照顾意味着花时间做那些有助于你生活得更好、改善你身体健康和心理健康的事情。这可以帮助你管理压力、降低患病风险并增加你的精力。即使是日常生活中微小的自我照顾行为也能产生很大的影响。以下是一些自我照顾的建议：定期锻炼。每天只需步行30分钟就能改善你的情绪并增进你的健康。少量的运动也会累积起来，所以如果你不能一次做30分钟，不要气馁。健康、规律的饮食并保持水分。均衡的饮食和充足的水分可以改善你一整天的精力和专注力。注意你摄入的咖啡因和酒精，以及它们如何影响你的情绪和身心健康——对一些人来说，减少咖啡因和酒精的摄入可能会有帮助。把睡眠放在优先位置。坚持作息时间表，并确保你获得足够的睡眠。来自设备和屏幕的蓝光会使入睡更加困难，因此在睡前减少来自手机或电脑的蓝光暴露。尝试一项放松活动。探索放松或健康项目或应用程序，其中可能包含冥想、肌肉放松或呼吸练习。为这些以及你喜欢的其他健康活动安排固定的时间，例如听音乐、阅读、在大自然中度过时光以及从事低压力的爱好。设定目标和优先事项。决定哪些必须现在完成，哪些可以等待。如果你开始觉得自己承担了太多，学会对新的任务说“不”。试着在一天结束时欣赏你已经完成的事情。练习感恩。每天提醒自己你感激的事情。要具体。把它们写下来或在脑海中回放。关注积极面。识别并挑战你的消极和无益的想法。保持联系。联系能够提供情感支持和实际帮助的朋友或家人。自我照顾对每个人来说都不同，重要的是找到你所需要的并且喜欢的。可能需要反复尝试才能发现最适合你的方式。了解更多关于身心健康的做法。

英文原文：
Self-care means taking the time to do things that help you live well and improve both your physical health and mental health. This can help you manage stress, lower your risk of illness, and increase your energy. Even small acts of self-care in your daily life can have a big impact.
Here are some self-care tips:
Get regular exercise. Just 30 minutes of walking every day can boost your mood and improve your health. Small amounts of exercise add up, so don’t be discouraged if you can’t do 30 minutes at one time.
Eat healthy, regular meals and stay hydrated. A balanced diet and plenty of water can improve your energy and focus throughout the day. Pay attention to your intake of caffeine and alcohol and how they affect your mood and well-being—for some, decreasing caffeine and alcohol consumption can be helpful.
Make sleep a priority . Stick to a schedule, and make sure you’re getting enough sleep. Blue light from devices and screens can make it harder to fall asleep, so reduce blue light exposure from your phone or computer before bedtime.
Try a relaxing activity. Explore relaxation or wellness programs or apps, which may incorporate meditation, muscle relaxation, or breathing exercises. Schedule regular times for these and other healthy activities you enjoy, such as listening to music, reading, spending time in nature, and engaging in low-stress hobbies.
Set goals and priorities. Decide what must get done now and what can wait. Learn to say “no” to new tasks if you start to feel like you’re taking on too much. Try to appreciate what you have accomplished at the end of the day.
Practice gratitude. Remind yourself daily of things you are grateful for. Be specific. Write them down or replay them in your mind.
Focus on positivity . Identify and challenge your negative and unhelpful thoughts.
Stay connected. Reach out to friends or family members who can provide emotional support and practical help.
Self-care looks different for everyone, and it is important to find what you need and enjoy. It may take trial and error to discover what works best for you.
Learn more about healthy practices for your mind and body .

Difficulty concentrating
Loss of interest in things you usually find enjoyable
Inability to complete usual tasks and activities
Feelings of irritability, frustration, or restlessness

They can refer you to a qualified mental health professional, such as a psychologist, psychiatrist, or clinical social worker, who can help you figure out the next steps. Find tips for talking with a health care provider about your mental health.
You can learn more about getting help on the NIMH website. You can also learn about finding support and locating mental health services in your area on the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration website.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
心理治疗（也称为谈话治疗）是指多种旨在帮助一个人识别并改变令人困扰的情绪、想法和行为的治疗方法。大多数心理治疗以一对一形式与持证心理健康专业人员进行，或在团体环境中与其他患者一起进行。心理治疗和药物是心理健康治疗最常见的形式。NIMH 有关于心理健康药物的信息。一般来说，心理治疗的目标是缓解症状、维持或增强日常功能，并改善生活质量。您或您认识的人可能出于许多原因寻求心理治疗，包括：应对来自工作或家庭情况的严重或长期压力、亲人离世，或关系或家庭问题；出现没有躯体解释的症状，例如睡眠或食欲变化、精力不足、对曾经享受的活动缺乏兴趣或愉悦感、持续易怒、过度担忧，或一种挥之不去的沮丧或绝望感；医疗服务提供者怀疑您患有或诊断您患有正在干扰您生活的精神障碍；支持被诊断患有影响其心理健康状况的儿童或家庭成员。首先由医疗服务提供者进行检查可以帮助排除身体健康问题。这一步很重要，因为有时症状，例如情绪变化或注意力难以集中，是由医学状况引起的。

英文原文：
Psychotherapy (also called talk therapy) refers to a variety of treatments that aim to help a person identify and change troubling emotions, thoughts, and behaviors. Most psychotherapy takes place one-on-one with a licensed mental health professional or with other patients in a group setting.
Psychotherapy and medication are the most common forms of mental health treatment. NIMH has information on mental health medications .
In general, the goals of psychotherapy are to gain relief from symptoms, maintain or enhance daily functioning, and improve quality of life.
You or someone you know might seek out psychotherapy for many reasons, including:
Dealing with severe or long-term stress from a job or family situation, the loss of a loved one, or relationship or family problems
Having symptoms with no physical explanation, such as changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, lack of interest or pleasure in activities you once enjoyed, persistent irritability, excessive worry, or a sense of discouragement or hopelessness that won’t go away
A health care provider suspecting you have or diagnosing you with a mental disorder that is interfering with your life
Supporting a child or family member who has been diagnosed with a condition affecting their mental health
First being examined by a health care provider can help rule out a physical health issue. This step is important because sometimes symptoms, like a change in mood or trouble concentrating, are due to a medical condition.

metadata.title: 心理治疗 / Psychotherapies
metadata.keywords: 心理治疗 心理咨询 认知行为疗法 CBT 咨询师
metadata.section: What is psychotherapy? / 定义 含义 什么是 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
心理治疗可作为药物治疗及其他治疗方案的替代或辅助手段。选择正确的治疗方案应基于个人的具体需求和医疗状况，并应在心理健康专业人员的指导下进行。即使药物能缓解症状，心理治疗仍有助于解决特定问题。这些问题可能包括自我挫败的思维方式；不合理的恐惧；与他人互动的问题；或难以应对家庭、学校或工作中的情况。

英文原文：
Psychotherapy can be used as an alternative to or alongside medication and other treatment options. Choosing the right treatment plan is based on a person's individual needs and medical situation and should occur under the guidance of a mental health professional.
Even when medication relieves symptoms, psychotherapy can help address specific issues. These might include self-defeating ways of thinking; irrational fears; problems interacting with other people; or difficulty coping with situations at home, school, or work.

metadata.title: 心理治疗 / Psychotherapies
metadata.keywords: 心理治疗 心理咨询 认知行为疗法 CBT 咨询师
metadata.section: Psychotherapy and other treatment options / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
多种心理治疗已被证明能有效治疗心理健康障碍。通常，治疗类型会根据具体障碍进行调整。例如，强迫症患者的治疗方法与双相障碍患者的治疗方法不同。治疗师可能采用一种主要方法，或根据其培训、所治疗的障碍以及接受治疗者的需求，融合多种方法的元素。心理治疗的要素可包括以下内容：帮助一个人意识到不准确或有害的自动思维方式（例如，对自己的能力评价过低），然后质疑这些想法，理解这些想法如何影响其情绪和行为，并改变自我挫败的行为模式。这种方法被称为认知行为疗法（CBT）。识别应对压力的方法并制定解决问题的策略。审视与他人的互动并教授社交和沟通技巧。应用正念和放松技巧，如冥想和呼吸练习。对焦虑障碍使用暴露疗法（一种CBT），即一个人在支持性环境中短暂停留，学习忍受某些物品、想法或想象场景引起的痛苦。随着时间的推移持续进行，直到与这些事物相关的恐惧降低。追踪情绪和行为，以提高对其相互影响的意识。使用支持性咨询来探讨困扰问题并获得情感支持。制定安全计划以帮助应对自残或自杀念头，识别警告信号，并使用应对策略，例如联系朋友、家人或紧急人员。心理治疗有很多类型。疗法通常是既有方法（如CBT）的变体。心理治疗没有像美国食品药品监督管理局对药物那样的正式批准程序。
然而，对于许多疗法，涉及大量患者的研究已提供证据表明该治疗有效。这些循证疗法已被证明可减轻抑郁、焦虑和其他精神障碍的症状。NIMH的健康主题页面列出了一些用于治疗特定障碍的循证疗法。

英文原文：
A variety of psychotherapies have been shown to effectively treat mental health disorders. Often, the type of treatment is tailored to the specific disorder. For example, the treatment approach for someone who has obsessive-compulsive disorder is different than the approach for someone who has bipolar disorder. Therapists may use one primary approach or incorporate elements from multiple approaches depending on their training, the disorder being treated, and the needs of the person receiving treatment.
Elements of psychotherapy can include the following:
Help a person become aware of automatic ways of thinking that are inaccurate or harmful (for example, having a low opinion of their abilities) and then question those thoughts, understand how the thoughts affect their emotions and behavior, and change self-defeating behavior patterns. This approach is known as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) .
Identify ways to cope with stress and develop problem-solving strategies.
Examine interactions with others and teach social and communication skills.
Apply mindfulness and relaxation techniques, such as meditation and breathing exercises.
Use exposure therapy (a type of CBT) for anxiety disorders, in which a person spends brief periods in a supportive environment learning to tolerate the distress caused by certain items, ideas, or imagined scenes. This is continued until, over time, the fear associated with those things goes down.
Track emotions and behaviors to raise awareness of their impact on each other.
Use supportive counseling to explore troubling issues and receive emotional support.
Create a safety plan to help with thoughts of self-harm or suicide, recognize warning signs, and use coping strategies, such as contacting friends, family, or emergency personnel.
There are many types of psychotherapy. Therapies are often variations of an established approach, such as CBT. There is no formal approval process for psychotherapies like there is for medications by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
However, for many therapies, research involving large numbers of patients has provided evidence that the treatment is effective. These evidence-based therapies have been shown to reduce symptoms of depression, anxiety, and other mental disorders. NIMH's health topic pages list some of the evidence-based therapies used to treat specific disorders.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
心理治疗师有不同的专业背景和专长。治疗师采用的方法取决于其培训、经验以及所治疗的障碍。本节及下一节提供的信息可帮助您查找治疗师的资质以及寻找治疗师的资源。一旦您确定了一位或多位可能的治疗师，初步交谈有助于您了解治疗将如何进行，以及您是否对治疗师感到自在。融洽与信任至关重要。治疗中的讨论极为私密，您对治疗师感到自在并对其专业能力有信心很重要。这些初步交谈可以当面、通过电话或线上进行。可考虑询问以下问题：治疗师的资质和经验是什么？治疗师有专长吗？治疗师将采用什么方法来帮助您？他们是否实践某种特定类型的治疗？该治疗的理论依据及其证据基础是什么？治疗师是否有诊断和治疗该年龄组（例如儿童）及特定病症的经验？如果患者是儿童，父母或照护者将如何参与治疗？治疗的目标是什么？治疗师是否建议特定的时间范围或次数？进展将如何评估？如果您（或治疗师）觉得您没有开始改善，会怎样？药物是否是一个选项？该治疗师能否开具药物？会谈是否保密？保密性如何保证？保密性是否存在限制？如果您接受治疗的时间已达到您认为合理的长度，但仍未见好转，请与您的治疗师谈谈。您可能想探索其他心理健康专业人员或方法。

英文原文：
Therapists have different professional backgrounds and specialties. The approach a therapist uses depends on their training and experience and the disorder being treated. This section and the next provide information that can help you find a therapist’s credentials and resources for locating therapists.
Once you have identified one or more possible therapists, a preliminary conversation can help you understand how treatment will proceed and if you feel comfortable with the therapist. Rapport and trust are essential. Discussions in therapy are deeply personal, and it’s important that you feel comfortable with the therapist and have confidence in their expertise. These preliminary conversations may happen in person, by phone, or virtually.
Consider asking the following questions:
What are the credentials and experience of the therapist? Does the therapist have a specialty?
What approach will the therapist use to help you? Do they practice a particular type of therapy? What is the rationale for the therapy and its evidence base?
Does the therapist have experience in diagnosing and treating the age group (for example, a child) and the specific condition? If the patient is a child, how will parents or caregivers be involved in treatment?
What are the goals of therapy? Does the therapist recommend a specific time frame or number of sessions? How will progress be assessed? What happens if you (or the therapist) feel you aren't starting to improve?
Are medications an option? Is this therapist able to prescribe medications?
Are meetings confidential? How is confidentiality assured? Are there limits to confidentiality?
If you have been in therapy for what feels like a reasonable amount of time and are not getting better, talk to your therapist. You might want to explore other mental health professionals or approaches.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
许多类型的专业人员提供心理治疗。例如包括精神科医生、心理学家、社会工作者、咨询师和精神科护士。关于提供者资质的信息可从全国精神疾病联盟和物质滥用与精神健康服务管理局获取。NIMH有关于获取帮助、寻找医疗保健提供者和获得治疗（包括减费医疗服务）方式的信息。您的健康保险提供者也可能有一份参与您计划的特定精神健康专业人员名单。在与潜在治疗师交谈时，询问治疗费用、治疗师是否接受保险，以及是否根据收入有浮动收费标准。以下专业组织在其网站上有用于寻找精神健康专业人员的名录或定位器：认知与行为治疗学会、美国儿童与青少年精神病学会、美国老年精神病学会、美国婚姻与家庭治疗学会、美国临床社会工作委员会、美国专业心理学委员会、美国精神病学协会、美国心理学会、行为与认知治疗协会、全国社会工作者协会、全国健康服务心理学家注册处、今日心理学、临床心理学学会。全国倡导组织提供关于寻找精神健康专业人员的信息，有些在其网站上有用于寻找治疗师的定位器。例如包括：美国焦虑与抑郁协会、注意力缺陷障碍协会、儿童与成人注意力缺陷/多动障碍组织、抑郁与双相支持联盟、国际强迫症基金会、美国精神健康、全国精神疾病联盟。注意：NIMH不评估这些网站上列出的个体从业者的专业资格和能力。这些资源仅供参考。它们不是完整名单，某个组织的列入不构成NIMH、美国国立卫生研究院、美国卫生与公众服务部或美国政府的认可。
许多大学或医学院设有附属项目，提供治疗选择，包括培训诊所。你可以通过搜索当地大学健康中心的网站，查找其精神病学或心理学系来找到这些项目。你也可以访问你所在州或县卫生部门的网站，查找他们可能提供的心理健康相关项目。

英文原文：
Many types of professionals offer psychotherapy. Examples include psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers, counselors, and psychiatric nurses. Information on providers’ credentials is available from the National Alliance on Mental Illness and the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration .
NIMH has information on ways to get help , find a health care provider, and access treatment, including reduced-cost health services. Your health insurance provider may also have a list of specific mental health professionals participating in your plan.
When talking with a prospective therapist, ask about treatment fees, whether the therapist accepts insurance, and whether there is a sliding scale for fees according to income.
The following professional organizations have directories or locators on their websites for finding mental health professionals:
Academy of Cognitive and Behavioral Therapies
American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
American Association for Geriatric Psychiatry
American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy
American Board of Clinical Social Work
American Board of Professional Psychology
American Psychiatric Association
American Psychological Association
Association for Behavioral and Cognitive Therapies
National Association of Social Workers
National Register of Health Service Psychologists
Psychology Today
Society of Clinical Psychology
National advocacy organizations provide information on finding mental health professionals, and some have locators for finding a therapist on their websites. Examples include:
Anxiety & Depression Association of America
Attention Deficit Disorder Association
Children and Adults With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance
International OCD Foundation
Mental Health America
National Alliance on Mental Illness
Note : NIMH does not evaluate the professional qualifications and competencies of individual practitioners listed on these websites. These resources are provided for informational purposes only. They are not comprehensive lists, and an organization’s inclusion does not constitute an endorsement by NIMH, the National Institutes of Health, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, or the U.S. government.
Many universities or medical schools have affiliated programs that offer treatment options, including training clinics. You can find these programs by searching the website of local university health centers for their psychiatry or psychology departments. You can also go to the website for the health department in your state or county to look for mental health-related programs they might offer.

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
注意缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）是一种神经发育障碍，其特征为：注意力不集中，例如难以集中注意力、持续完成任务或保持条理；多动，例如经常四处走动（包括在不适当的场合）、感到坐立不安或过度说话；冲动，例如打断他人、侵扰他人或难以等待轮到自己。对一些人来说，注意力不集中的症状最为突出，而另一些人则在多动和冲动方面困难最大。有些人则在所有三个方面都出现症状。人们有时表现出这些行为是常见的。然而，对于ADHD患者来说，这些行为频繁发生，并出现在多种情境中，如在学校、家里、工作中或与家人和朋友相处时，且干扰日常生活。

英文原文：
ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by:
Inattention, such as having difficulty paying attention, keeping on task, or staying organized
Hyperactivity, such as often moving around (including during inappropriate times), feeling restless, or talking excessively
Impulsivity, such as interrupting, intruding on others, or having trouble waiting one’s turn
For some people, inattention symptoms are the strongest, while other people have the most difficulty with hyperactivity and impulsivity. Some people experience symptoms in all three areas.
It is common for people to show these behaviors some of the time. However, for people with ADHD, the behaviors are frequent and occur across multiple situations, such as at school, at home, at work, or with family and friends and interfere with daily life.

metadata.title: 注意缺陷多动障碍 / Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
metadata.keywords: 注意缺陷多动障碍 ADHD 注意力 执行功能
metadata.section: What is ADHD? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
注意缺陷多动障碍是儿童中最常被诊断的障碍之一。症状始于童年，通常持续到青少年期和成年期。注意缺陷多动障碍常与其他障碍和状况共病，如破坏性行为、学习障碍、睡眠问题、焦虑或抑郁，这会使这些状况更难诊断和治疗。对许多注意缺陷多动障碍患者来说，症状会在日常生活中造成问题。症状可能使人难以完成任务；干扰学校、工作或其他活动；并使社会关系紧张。注意缺陷多动障碍儿童受伤、社交问题、家庭压力和成绩差的风险增加。注意缺陷多动障碍青少年和成人更可能从事危险行为，如物质使用和不安全性行为，并且工作表现差和财务问题的风险增加。

英文原文：
ADHD is one of the most common disorders diagnosed in children. Symptoms begin in childhood and usually continue into the teen years and adulthood. ADHD often co-occurs with other disorders and conditions, such as disruptive behavior, learning disorders, sleep problems, anxiety , or depression , which can make the conditions harder to diagnose and treat.
For many people with ADHD, symptoms cause problems in daily life. Symptoms can make it hard to get things done; interfere with school, work, or other activities; and strain social relationships. Children with ADHD are at increased risk for injuries, social problems, family stress, and poor grades. Teens and adults with ADHD are more likely to engage in risky behaviors, such as substance use and unsafe sexual activity, and are at increased risk for poor job performance and financial problems.

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
双相障碍（曾被称为躁狂抑郁性精神病或躁狂抑郁症）是一种精神疾病，会导致一个人的情绪、精力、活动水平和注意力发生明显变化。双相障碍患者常经历极度“高涨”、欣快、易怒或精力旺盛的行为时期（称为躁狂发作）以及非常“低落”、悲伤、冷漠或绝望的时期（称为抑郁发作）。

英文原文：
Bipolar disorder (formerly called manic-depressive illness or manic depression) is a mental illness that causes clear shifts in a person’s mood, energy, activity levels, and concentration. People with bipolar disorder often experience periods of extremely “up,” elated, irritable, or energized behavior (known as manic episodes) and very “down,” sad, indifferent, or hopeless periods (known as depressive episodes).

metadata.title: 双相障碍 / Bipolar Disorder
metadata.keywords: 双相障碍 躁狂 心境 情绪波动
metadata.section: What is bipolar disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
双相障碍的症状可能对一个人的心理和身体健康带来严重挑战。双相障碍患者常伴有其他精神障碍，部分人可能出现精神病性症状，如幻觉或妄想。这些症状可能干扰日常活动、人际关系以及工作或学业责任。有些人还可能因自身症状而遭遇污名，这可能使他们不愿寻求所需的帮助。双相障碍通常需要终身治疗，但有效的治疗计划可以帮助人们管理症状并改善生活质量。

英文原文：
The symptoms of bipolar disorder can impose serious challenges to a person’s mental and physical health. People with bipolar disorder often have other mental disorders, and some people may experience symptoms of psychosis , such as hallucinations or delusions. The symptoms can interfere with everyday activities, relationships, and work or school responsibilities. Some people may also experience stigma related to their symptoms, which can keep them from seeking the help they need.
Bipolar disorder usually requires lifelong treatment, but an effective treatment plan can help people manage their symptoms and improve their quality of life.

英文原文：
Borderline personality disorder is a mental illness that severely impacts a person’s ability to regulate their emotions. This loss of emotional control can increase impulsivity, affect how a person feels about themselves, and negatively impact their relationships with others.

metadata.title: 边缘型人格障碍 / Borderline Personality Disorder
metadata.keywords: 边缘型人格障碍 情绪调节 人际关系
metadata.section: What is borderline personality disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
边缘型人格障碍可对一个人的人际关系和情绪健康造成重大挑战。边缘型人格障碍患者更可能发生自伤。他们还可能经历抑郁症、创伤后应激障碍、双相障碍、焦虑障碍、物质使用障碍或进食障碍的症状。这些挑战可导致显著痛苦和较低的生活质量。有效的治疗可帮助边缘型人格障碍患者管理其症状、支持其健康并改善其日常功能。

英文原文：
Borderline personality disorder can cause significant challenges to a person’s relationships and emotional well-being. People with borderline personality disorder are more likely to engage in self-harm. They may also experience symptoms of depression , post-traumatic stress disorder , bipolar disorder , anxiety disorders , substance use disorder , or eating disorders .
These challenges can lead to significant distress and a lower quality of life. Effective treatments can help people with borderline personality disorder manage their symptoms, support their well-being, and improve their daily functioning.

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
进食障碍是严重的疾病，其特征是人的进食行为出现严重紊乱。尽管许多人可能偶尔会担心自己的健康、体重或外貌，但有些人会变得执着或痴迷于减肥、体重或体型，以及控制食物摄入。这些可能是进食障碍的迹象。

英文原文：
Eating disorders are serious illnesses marked by severe disturbances in a person’s eating behaviors. Although many people may be concerned about their health, weight, or appearance on occasion, some become fixated or obsessed with weight loss, body weight or shape, and controlling their food intake. These may be signs of an eating disorder.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
进食障碍是严重的，可能危及生命。此外，进食障碍患者发生医学并发症和共病精神疾病的风险更高，包括抑郁、焦虑和物质使用障碍。这些共病状况可使进食障碍恶化。进食障碍可以成功治疗。早期发现和治疗对于完全康复很重要。

英文原文：
Eating disorders are serious and can be life-threatening. In addition, people with eating disorders are at higher risk for medical complications and co-occurring mental illnesses, including depression , anxiety , and substance use disorders . These co-occurring conditions can make eating disorders worse. Eating disorders can be treated successfully. Early detection and treatment are important for a full recovery.

强迫症（OCD）是一种以无法控制和反复出现的想法（强迫思维）、重复且过度的行为（强迫行为），或两者兼有为特征的障碍。强迫症症状可在任何时间开始，但通常始于童年晚期至成年早期之间。

英文原文：
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a disorder marked by uncontrollable and recurring thoughts (obsessions), repetitive and excessive behaviors (compulsions), or both. OCD symptoms can begin any time but usually start between late childhood and young adulthood.

documents.content:

强迫症的症状常常耗费时间，并可能导致显著的痛苦或干扰日常生活。强迫症患者也常被诊断患有心境障碍或焦虑障碍。尽管强迫症无法治愈，但现有的治疗可以帮助患者管理症状、参与日常活动并改善生活质量。

英文原文：
OCD symptoms are often time-consuming and can cause significant distress or interfere with daily life. It is common for people with OCD also to have a diagnosed mood or anxiety disorder . Although there is no cure for OCD, available treatments can help people manage their symptoms, participate in day-to-day activities, and improve their quality of life.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
精神分裂症是一种严重的精神疾病，影响一个人的思维、感受和行为。精神分裂症患者可能看起来似乎与现实脱节，这可能对他们及其家人和朋友造成痛苦。人们通常在16至30岁之间首次被诊断为精神分裂症，即在首次精神病发作之后。

英文原文：
Schizophrenia is a serious mental illness that affects how a person thinks, feels, and behaves. People with schizophrenia may seem as though they have lost touch with reality, which can be distressing for them and for their family and friends. People are usually first diagnosed with schizophrenia between the ages of 16 and 30, after the first episode of psychosis .

metadata.title: 精神分裂症 / Schizophrenia
metadata.keywords: 精神分裂症 幻觉 妄想 精神病性症状
metadata.section: What is schizophrenia? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
精神分裂症的症状可能使人难以参与日常活动，许多精神分裂症患者面临重大的健康、社会和经济挑战。精神分裂症患者常常在症状出现与开始治疗之间经历延迟，这可能影响他们对治疗的反应，并导致长期健康状况和福祉恶化。研究表明，在首次精神病发作之前，思维、情绪和社会功能的逐渐变化往往已经出现。在首次发作之前识别这些微妙变化并让人们接受治疗，可能对他们的健康、福祉和日常功能产生长期益处。治疗可以帮助精神分裂症患者参与学习或工作、实现独立并享受人际关系。

英文原文：
Schizophrenia symptoms can make it difficult to participate in everyday activities and many people with schizophrenia face significant health, social, and economic challenges. People with schizophrenia often experience a delay between the onset of symptoms and the start of treatment, which can impact their response to treatment and lead to worse health and well-being over the long term.
Research shows that gradual changes in thinking, mood, and social functioning often appear before the first episode of psychosis. Identifying these subtle changes and connecting people with treatment before their first episode could have long-term benefits for their health, well-being, and daily functioning. Treatment can help people with schizophrenia engage in school or work, achieve independence, and enjoy personal relationships.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
人们在经历或目睹创伤性事件后，可能会有多种反应，例如自然灾害、暴力行为或严重事故。常见的反应包括感到焦虑、悲伤或愤怒；难以集中注意力和入睡；以及反复思考所发生的事情。大多数人会从这些症状中恢复，他们的反应会随着时间推移而减轻。如果症状在创伤性事件后持续较长时间，并开始干扰日常生活的各个方面，如人际关系或工作，则可能被诊断为创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。患有PTSD的人可能即使并未处于危险之中，仍会持续感到紧张或恐惧。

英文原文：
People may have a range of reactions after experiencing or witnessing a traumatic event, such as a natural disaster, act of violence, or serious accident. Common reactions include feeling anxious, sad, or angry; having trouble concentrating and sleeping; and thinking about what happened. Most people will recover from these symptoms , and their reactions will lessen over time.
People may be diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) if their symptoms last for an extended period after a traumatic event and begin to interfere with aspects of daily life, such as relationships or work. People who have PTSD may continue to feel stressed or frightened, even though they are not in danger.

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Traumatic Events and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: What is PTSD? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
创伤后应激障碍的症状可造成显著痛苦，并妨碍一个人从事日常活动的能力，包括睡眠和进食。创伤后应激障碍患者常共病其他状况，如抑郁症、物质使用或焦虑障碍。创伤性事件的某些方面以及某些生物和社会因素可能使一些人更易发生创伤后应激障碍。例如，既往暴露于逆境和其他创伤性经历，尤其是在童年期，可增加一个人日后发生创伤后应激障碍的机会。虽然许多经历过危险事件的人最初会出现一些症状，但大多数人不会发生创伤后应激障碍——多种因素在起作用。

英文原文：
The symptoms of PTSD can cause significant distress and interfere with a person’s ability to engage in daily activities, including sleeping and eating. People with PTSD often have co-occurring conditions, such as depression , substance use , or anxiety disorders .
Aspects of the traumatic event and certain biological and social factors may make some people more likely to develop PTSD. For instance, previous exposure to adversity and other traumatic experiences, especially in childhood, can increase a person’s chance of developing PTSD later in life. While many people who live through a dangerous event experience some symptoms initially, most do not develop PTSD—multiple factors play a part.

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Traumatic Events and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: Why is NIMH studying PTSD? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
创伤事件是指令人震惊、恐惧或危险的经历，可能在情感和身体上对某人造成影响。创伤事件可包括自然灾害（如飓风、地震和洪水）、暴力行为（如袭击、虐待、恐怖袭击和大规模枪击）以及车祸或其他事故等经历。在创伤情境期间和之后感到害怕是自然的。恐惧是身体“战斗或逃跑”反应的一部分，这种反应帮助我们避免或应对潜在危险。人们在创伤后可能会经历一系列反应，包括：感到焦虑、悲伤或愤怒；难以集中注意力和入睡；不断回想所发生的事。大多数人会从这些症状中恢复，他们的反应会随时间减轻。那些持续经历症状的人可能被诊断为创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。如果症状随时间没有改善或开始干扰日常生活，寻求专业帮助很重要。一个人可能需要帮助的一些迹象包括：过度担忧或感到非常焦虑、悲伤或恐惧；经常哭泣；难以清晰思考；有令人恐惧的想法或闪回，重新体验该经历；感到愤怒、怨恨或易怒；做噩梦或难以入睡；回避会带回令人不安的记忆和反应的地方或人；与家人和朋友变得孤立。对创伤的身体反应也可能意味着一个人需要帮助。身体症状可能包括：头痛；胃痛和消化问题；难以入睡或保持睡眠；心跳加速和出汗；非常紧张不安且容易受惊。有精神疾病或物质使用个人史或家族史的人、既往暴露于创伤经历的人、面临持续压力或创伤（如虐待）的人，或缺乏朋友和家人支持的人，可能更有可能出现更严重的症状并需要额外帮助。经历创伤事件的人也可能经历惊恐障碍、抑郁、物质使用或自杀念头。针对这些状况的治疗可以帮助创伤后的恢复。

英文原文：
A traumatic event is a shocking, scary, or dangerous experience that can affect someone emotionally and physically. Traumatic events can include experiences such as natural disasters (such as hurricanes, earthquakes, and floods), acts of violence (such as assault, abuse, terror attacks, and mass shootings), and car crashes or other accidents.
It is natural to feel afraid during and after a traumatic situation. Fear is a part of the body’s “fight-or-flight” response, which helps us avoid or respond to potential danger. People may experience a range of reactions after trauma, including:
Feeling anxious, sad, or angry
Trouble concentrating and sleeping
Continually thinking about what happened
Most people will recover from these symptoms, and their reactions will lessen over time. Those who continue to experience symptoms may be diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) .
It is important to seek professional help if symptoms do not improve over time or begin to interfere with daily life. Some signs that a person may need help include:
Worrying a lot or feeling very anxious, sad, or fearful
Crying often
Having trouble thinking clearly
Having frightening thoughts or flashbacks, reliving the experience
Feeling angry, resentful, or irritable
Having nightmares or difficulty sleeping
Avoiding places or people that bring back disturbing memories and responses
Becoming isolated from family and friends
Physical responses to trauma may also mean that a person needs help. Physical symptoms may include:
Having headaches
Having stomach pain and digestive issues
Having difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep
Having a racing heart and sweating
Being very jumpy and easily startled
People who have a personal or family history of mental illness or substance use, who have had previous exposure to traumatic experiences, who face ongoing stress or trauma (such as abuse), or who lack support from friends and family may be more likely to develop more severe symptoms and need additional help.
People who experience traumatic events also may experience panic disorder , depression , substance use , or suicidal thoughts . Treatment for these conditions can help with recovery after trauma.

metadata.title: 应对创伤事件 / Coping With Traumatic Events
metadata.keywords: 应对创伤事件 灾难 恢复 陪伴
metadata.section: How do people respond to traumatic events? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
儿童对创伤事件可能产生极端反应，但其症状可能与成人所见的症状不同。在6岁以下的儿童中，症状可能包括：在学会使用厕所后尿床；忘记如何说话或无法说话；在游戏时间中重演可怕事件；对父母或其他成人异常粘人。年龄较大的儿童和青少年通常表现出的症状更类似于成人所见的症状。他们还可能出现破坏性、不尊重或毁灭性的行为。年龄较大的儿童和青少年可能因未能防止受伤或死亡而感到内疚，或产生报复的念头。

英文原文：
Children can have extreme reactions to traumatic events, but their symptoms may not be the same as those seen in adults. In children younger than age 6, symptoms can include:
Wetting the bed after having learned to use the toilet
Forgetting how to talk or being unable to talk
Acting out the scary event during playtime
Being unusually clingy with a parent or other adult
Older children and teens usually show symptoms more like those seen in adults. They may also develop disruptive, disrespectful, or destructive behaviors. Older children and teens may feel guilt over not preventing injury or death or have thoughts of revenge.

metadata.title: 应对创伤事件 / Coping With Traumatic Events
metadata.keywords: 应对创伤事件 灾难 恢复 陪伴
metadata.section: How do children and teens react to trauma? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
健康的应对方式有助于减轻压力并改善身心健康。以下是一些你可以为自己做的事情：避免使用酒精或药物与支持你的可信赖的朋友和家人共度时光尽量保持用餐、锻炼和睡眠的规律进行锻炼、正念或其他有助于减轻压力的活动设定现实的目标，并专注于你能应对的事情了解自我照顾策略以及何时寻求专业帮助。

英文原文：
Healthy ways of coping can help reduce stress and improve well-being. Here are some things you can do to help yourself:
Avoid the use of alcohol or drugs
Spend time with trusted friends and relatives who are supportive
Try to maintain routines for meals, exercise, and sleep
Engage in exercise, mindfulness, or other activities that help reduce stress
Set realistic goals and focus on what you can manage
Learn about self-care strategies and when to seek professional help .

metadata.title: 应对创伤事件 / Coping With Traumatic Events
metadata.keywords: 应对创伤事件 灾难 恢复 陪伴
metadata.section: What can I do to cope after a traumatic event? / 自我照顾 应对 调节

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
如果你对自己的心理健康有顾虑，请与初级保健提供者交谈。他们可以将你转介给合格的心理健康专业人员，如心理学家、精神科医生或临床社会工作者，他们可以帮助你确定下一步。查找与医疗保健提供者谈论心理健康的提示。你可以在NIMH网站上了解更多关于获得帮助的信息。你还可以在药物滥用和心理健康服务管理局（SAMHSA）网站上了解如何在您所在地区寻找支持和定位心理健康服务。此外，SAMHSA的灾难求助热线为经历与自然或人为灾难相关的情绪困扰的人们提供危机咨询和支持。该热线免费、多语言、保密，并且每天24小时、每周7天可用。

英文原文：
If you have concerns about your mental health, talk to a primary care provider. They can refer you to a qualified mental health professional, such as a psychologist, psychiatrist, or clinical social worker, who can help you figure out the next steps. Find tips for talking with a health care provider about your mental health .
You can learn more about getting help o n the NIMH website. You can also learn about finding support and locating mental health services in your area on the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) website.
In addition, SAMHSA’s Disaster Distress Helpline provides crisis counseling and support to people experiencing emotional distress related to natural or human-caused disasters. The helpline is free, multilingual, confidential, and available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

metadata.title: 应对创伤事件 / Coping With Traumatic Events
metadata.keywords: 应对创伤事件 灾难 恢复 陪伴
metadata.section: How can I find help for coping with traumatic events? / 求助 支持 咨询师 自我照顾 应对 调节

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
偶尔感到焦虑是生活的正常组成部分。许多人会担心健康、金钱、学业、工作或家庭等事情。但广泛性焦虑障碍（GAD）患者对这些事情及其他事情感到极度担忧或紧张的频率更高或强度更大——即使这种担忧与情境不相称。GAD通常涉及一种持续存在的焦虑或恐惧感，会干扰你的生活方式。它不同于偶尔担心事情或因压力性生活事件而感到焦虑。对于GAD患者，这些焦虑感可能持续数月甚至数年。GAD逐渐发展，通常始于成年早期，尽管它可能发生在任何年龄。女性比男性更可能经历GAD，一些女性在孕期和产后期间经历它。通过正确的治疗和支持，GAD患者可以管理他们的焦虑并改善生活质量。

英文原文：
Occasional anxiety is a normal part of life. Many people worry about things such as health, money, school, work, or family. But people with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) feel extremely worried or nervous more frequently or more intensely about these and other things—even when the worry is out of proportion with the situation.
GAD usually involves a persistent feeling of anxiety or dread that interferes with how you live your life. It is not the same as occasionally worrying about things or experiencing anxiety due to stressful life events. For people with GAD, these feelings of anxiety can last for months or even years.
GAD develops gradually and usually starts in early adulthood, although it can occur at any age. Women are more likely than men to experience GAD, with some women experiencing it during pregnancy and the postpartum period. With the right treatment and support, people with GAD can manage their anxiety and improve their quality of life.

metadata.title: 广泛性焦虑 / Generalized Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 广泛性焦虑 过度担心 GAD
metadata.section: What is generalized anxiety disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
广泛性焦虑障碍患者可能会：对日常事务过度担忧；难以控制自己的担忧或紧张情绪；经常感到易怒或“坐立不安”；感到烦躁不安或难以放松；难以集中注意力；难以入睡或保持睡眠，或感到疲劳；经历头痛、肌肉酸痛、胃痛或紧张等疼痛；颤抖或抽搐；大量出汗、感到头晕或呼吸急促；吞咽困难；频繁上厕所。患有广泛性焦虑障碍的成年人常常对日常情况高度紧张，例如：工作保障或工作表现；健康；财务状况；子女或其他家庭成员的健康与福祉；迟到；完成家务和其他责任。患有广泛性焦虑障碍的儿童和青少年可能会担忧与成年人许多相同的事情，但他们的担忧往往集中在学校、课外活动、友谊和未来上。他们可能难以应对不确定性、害怕犯错，或担心让他人失望。患有广泛性焦虑障碍的儿童和青少年可能会力求完美，以此作为管理焦虑的一种方式。对于所有广泛性焦虑障碍患者，症状可能随时间波动，并且在压力时期往往更严重——例如，在身体患病、学校考试或家庭或关系冲突期间。

英文原文：
People with GAD may:
Worry excessively about everyday things
Have trouble controlling their worries or feelings of nervousness
Feel irritable or “on edge” frequently
Feel restless or have trouble relaxing
Have a hard time concentrating
Have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, or feel fatigued
Experience pain such as headaches, muscle aches, stomachaches, or tension
Tremble or twitch
Sweat a lot, feel lightheaded, or feel out of breath
Have a hard time swallowing
Make frequent trips to the bathroom
Adults with GAD are often highly nervous about everyday circumstances, such as:
Job security or performance
Health
Finances
The health and well-being of their children or other family members
Being late
Completing household chores and other responsibilities
Children and teens with GAD may worry about many of the same things as adults, but their concerns often center on school, extracurricular activities, friendships, and the future. They may struggle with uncertainty, fear of making mistakes, or worry about disappointing others. Children and teens with GAD may strive for perfection as a way to manage their anxiety.
For all people with GAD, symptoms may fluctuate over time and are often worse during times of stress—for example, during a physical illness, school exams, or a family or relationship conflict.

metadata.title: 广泛性焦虑 / Generalized Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 广泛性焦虑 过度担心 GAD
metadata.section: What are the signs and symptoms of generalized anxiety disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
广泛性焦虑 / 广泛性焦虑障碍：你需要了解的内容

这是正常的压力还是焦虑障碍？

生活可能充满压力——一个人可能会因为繁重的工作、学校的演出或生活中的变故而感到有压力。每个人都会时不时感到压力。压力是对外部原因的身体或心理反应，例如有很多作业或患有疾病。压力源可能是一次性或短期的发生，也可能在长时间内反复发生。焦虑是身体对压力的反应，即使当前没有威胁也可能发生。虽然偶尔的压力和焦虑是正常的，但它们不应控制你的生活。如果焦虑没有消失并开始干扰你的日常活动，你可能患有焦虑障碍。了解更多关于压力的信息。

英文原文：
Life can be stressful—a person may feel stressed about a demanding job, a performance at school, or a life change. Everyone feels stress from time to time.
Stress is the physical or mental response to an external cause, such as having a lot of homework or having an illness. A stressor may be a one-time or short-term occurrence, or it can happen repeatedly over a long time.
Anxiety is the body's reaction to stress and can occur even if there is no current threat.
While occasional stress and anxiety are normal, they shouldn’t control your life. If anxiety doesn’t go away and begins to interfere with your daily activities, you may have an anxiety disorder. Learn more about stress .

metadata.title: 广泛性焦虑 / Generalized Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 广泛性焦虑 过度担心 GAD
metadata.section: Is it normal stress or an anxiety disorder? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
广泛性焦虑障碍可能在家族中遗传，但该障碍的确切病因尚不清楚。研究表明，广泛性焦虑障碍由遗传、脑化学、生物学和环境因素共同导致。研究人员发现，外部原因，如经历创伤性事件或处于压力环境中，可能使个体发展为广泛性焦虑障碍的风险更高。

英文原文：
GAD may run in families, but the exact cause of the disorder is unknown. Research suggests that GAD results from a mix of genetics, brain chemistry, biology, and environment. Researchers have found that external causes, such as experiencing a traumatic event or being in a stressful environment, may put a person at higher risk for developing GAD.

metadata.title: 广泛性焦虑 / Generalized Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 广泛性焦虑 过度担心 GAD
metadata.section: What causes generalized anxiety disorder? / 影响因素 风险因素

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
要被诊断为广泛性焦虑障碍（GAD），一个人必须在至少6个月的大多数日子里感到难以控制担忧。他们还须至少具有以下症状中的三项：感到不安或“紧张不安”、疲劳、注意力难以集中、易怒、肌肉紧张或睡眠问题。如果你认为自己正在经历广泛性焦虑障碍的症状，请与医疗保健提供者交谈，例如初级保健医生、精神科医生、心理学家或临床社会工作者。在就诊期间，提供者可能会询问你的症状何时开始、持续了多长时间、出现的频率以及对你生活的影响。在讨论你的病史后，提供者可能会进行体格检查，以确保不是无关的身体问题导致你的症状。

英文原文：
To be diagnosed with GAD, a person must find it difficult to control worry on most days for at least 6 months. They must also have at least three of these symptoms: feeling restless or “on edge,” fatigue, trouble concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, or problems with sleep.
If you think you’re experiencing symptoms of GAD, talk to a health care provider, such as a primary care doctor, psychiatrist, psychologist, or clinical social worker. During the visit, the provider may ask when your symptoms began, how long they have lasted, how often they occur, and their impact on your life. After discussing your history, the provider may conduct a physical exam to ensure that an unrelated physical problem is not causing your symptoms.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
一些广泛性焦虑障碍患者还伴有其他精神或躯体健康障碍或状况，包括抑郁、其他焦虑障碍、创伤后应激障碍、慢性疼痛综合征、心血管问题，或自杀意念或行为。广泛性焦虑障碍也常与酒精和物质滥用相关。多种障碍并存可使治疗更为复杂，而广泛性焦虑障碍共病精神障碍的患者可能受益于一项涵盖其心理健康各个方面的综合治疗计划。

英文原文：
Some people with GAD have other mental and physical health disorders or conditions, including depression, other anxiety disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, chronic pain syndromes, cardiovascular problems, or suicidal thoughts or behaviors. GAD is also commonly associated with alcohol and substance misuse.
The presence of multiple disorders can make treatment more complex, and people with GAD and co-occurring mental disorders may benefit from a comprehensive treatment plan that addresses all aspects of their mental health.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
广泛性焦虑障碍的治疗通常包括心理治疗、药物治疗或两者兼有。选择正确的治疗方案基于个人的需求、偏好和医疗状况，以及与心理健康专业人员或医疗保健提供者的咨询。找到最佳治疗可能需要反复尝试，且心理治疗和药物治疗可能需要一些时间才能起效。

英文原文：
GAD treatment typically involves psychotherapy, medication, or both. Choosing the right treatment plan is based on a person’s needs, preferences, and medical situation, as well as consultation with a mental health professional or a health care provider. Finding the best treatment may take trial and error, and psychotherapy and medication can take some time to work.

metadata.title: 广泛性焦虑 / Generalized Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 广泛性焦虑 过度担心 GAD
metadata.section: How is generalized anxiety disorder treated? / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
心理治疗（也称为谈话治疗或咨询）在面对面或通过远程医疗虚拟进行时均可有效。提供者可能使用数字或移动技术（如应用程序或其他工具）来支持或补充治疗。不同的疗法适用于不同类型的人。认知行为疗法（CBT）是一种有研究支持的心理治疗类型，常用于治疗广泛性焦虑障碍。CBT帮助人们意识到不准确或有害的自动思维方式，然后质疑这些想法，理解这些想法如何影响他们的情绪和行为，并改变自我挫败的行为模式，以减少焦虑和担忧。CBT已得到充分研究，是心理治疗的“金标准”选择。广泛性焦虑障碍的另一种治疗选择是接纳与承诺疗法（ACT）。ACT采用与CBT不同的方法，鼓励对想法和行为采取非评判性的接纳，并促进参与有意义的活动。ACT使用正念和目标设定等策略来减少个人的不适和焦虑。越来越多的研究证明其对治疗广泛性焦虑障碍的有效性。了解更多关于心理治疗的信息。

英文原文：
Psychotherapy (also called talk therapy or counseling) can be effective when delivered in person or virtually via telehealth. A provider may support or supplement therapy using digital or mobile technology, like apps or other tools. Different therapies work for different types of people.
Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), a research-supported type of psychotherapy, is commonly used to treat GAD. CBT helps people become aware of automatic ways of thinking that are inaccurate or harmful and then question those thoughts, understand how the thoughts affect their emotions and behavior, and change self-defeating behavior patterns to feel less anxious and worried. CBT has been well studied and is the “gold standard” choice for psychotherapy.
Another treatment option for GAD is acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT). ACT takes a different approach than CBT, encouraging nonjudgmental acceptance of thoughts and behaviors and promoting engagement in meaningful activities. ACT uses strategies such as mindfulness and goal setting to reduce a person’s discomfort and anxiety. There is a growing body of research demonstrating its effectiveness for treating GAD.
Learn more about psychotherapy .

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
一些焦虑障碍患者通过加入自助或支持小组，与他人分享自己的问题和成就而获益。支持小组有面对面和在线两种形式。然而，你从支持小组成员那里得到的任何建议都应谨慎使用，并且不能替代医疗保健提供者的治疗建议。

英文原文：
Some people with anxiety disorders benefit from joining a self-help or support group and sharing their problems and achievements with others. Support groups are available both in person and online. However, any advice you receive from a support group member should be used cautiously and does not replace treatment recommendations from a health care provider.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
践行健康的生活方式也有助于对抗焦虑，尽管仅靠这一点不能替代治疗。研究人员发现，在日常生活中采取某些健康选择——例如减少咖啡因摄入和获得充足睡眠——当与标准治疗（如心理治疗和药物治疗）配合时，可以减轻焦虑症状。压力管理技巧，如运动、正念和冥想，也可以减轻焦虑症状并增强心理治疗的效果。您可以与医疗保健提供者交谈，了解更多关于这些技巧如何有益于您的治疗。了解更多维护心理健康的方法。

英文原文：
Practicing a healthy lifestyle also can help combat anxiety, although this alone cannot replace treatment. Researchers have found that implementing certain healthy choices in daily life—such as reducing caffeine intake and getting enough sleep—can reduce anxiety symptoms when paired with standard care—such as psychotherapy and medication.
Stress management techniques, such as exercise, mindfulness, and meditation, also can reduce anxiety symptoms and enhance the effects of psychotherapy. You can learn more about how these techniques benefit your treatment by talking with a health care provider.
Learn more ways to take care of your mental health .

A good way to help yourself or a loved one who may be struggling with GAD is to seek information. Research the signs and symptoms, learn about treatment options, and keep up to date with current research.

如果您对自己的心理健康有顾虑，请与初级保健提供者交谈。他们可以将您转介给合格的心理健康专业人员，例如心理学家、精神科医生或临床社会工作者，他们可以帮助您确定下一步。查找与医疗保健提供者谈论心理健康的提示。您可以在NIMH网站上了解更多关于获得帮助的信息。您还可以在药物滥用和心理健康服务管理局（SAMHSA）网站上了解如何寻找支持以及查找您所在地区的心理健康服务。

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
惊恐障碍患者会频繁且意外地出现惊恐发作。这些发作的特征是突然涌现的恐惧或不适感，或一种失控感，即使没有明确的危险或诱因。并非每个经历过惊恐发作的人都会发展为惊恐障碍。惊恐发作常包括一些身体症状，可能感觉像心脏病发作，例如身体颤抖或刺痛，或心率加快。惊恐发作可在任何时间发生，有时甚至在睡眠中。许多惊恐障碍患者担心可能再次发作，并可能显著改变自己的生活以避免再次发作。惊恐发作的频率可以是每天数次，也可以是一年数次。惊恐障碍通常始于青少年晚期或成年早期。女性比男性更易发展为惊恐障碍。通过正确的治疗和支持，惊恐障碍患者可以管理自己的症状并改善生活质量。

英文原文：
People with panic disorder have frequent and unexpected panic attacks. These attacks are characterized by a sudden wave of fear or discomfort or a sense of losing control even when there is no clear danger or trigger. Not everyone who experiences a panic attack will develop panic disorder.
Panic attacks often include physical symptoms that might feel like a heart attack, such as trembling or tingling in the body or a rapid heart rate. Panic attacks can occur at any time, sometimes even during sleep. Many people with panic disorder worry about the possibility of having another attack and may significantly change their lives to avoid having another attack. Panic attacks can occur as frequently as several times a day or as rarely as a few times a year.
Panic disorder often begins in the late teens or early adulthood. Women are more likely than men to develop panic disorder. With the right treatment and support, people with panic disorder can manage their symptoms and improve their quality of life.

metadata.title: 惊恐障碍 / Panic Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 惊恐障碍 惊恐发作 心慌 恐慌
metadata.section: What is panic disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
惊恐障碍患者可能会出现：突然且反复发作的、伴有极度焦虑和恐惧的惊恐发作；一种失控感；在惊恐发作期间对死亡或厄运将至的恐惧；对下一次惊恐发作何时发生的强烈担忧；对过去发生过惊恐发作的场所的恐惧或回避。惊恐发作期间的身体症状可能包括：心脏猛烈跳动或心跳加速；出汗；发冷；颤抖；呼吸困难；无力或头晕；手部刺痛或麻木；胸痛；胃痛或恶心。一次惊恐发作可持续几分钟至一小时，有时更长。虽然这些感受可能令人痛苦，但惊恐发作本身并不危及生命，身体症状通常会随时间缓解。然而，对某些人来说，对未来发作的恐惧可能导致持续的焦虑。

英文原文：
People with panic disorder may have:
Sudden and repeated panic attacks of overwhelming anxiety and fear
A feeling of being out of control
A fear of death or impending doom during a panic attack
An intense worry about when the next panic attack will happen
A fear or avoidance of places where panic attacks have occurred in the past
Physical symptoms during a panic attack may include:
Pounding or racing heart
Sweating
Chills
Trembling
Difficulty breathing
Weakness or dizziness
Tingly or numb hands
Chest pain
Stomach pain or nausea
A panic attack can last from a few minutes to an hour or sometimes longer. While these feelings can be distressing, panic attacks themselves are not life-threatening, and the physical symptoms usually resolve with time. However, for some, the fear of future attacks may lead to ongoing anxiety.

metadata.title: 惊恐障碍 / Panic Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 惊恐障碍 惊恐发作 心慌 恐慌
metadata.section: What are the signs and symptoms of panic disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
惊恐发作是一次性或偶发的强烈恐惧发作，伴有身体和情绪症状。孤立的惊恐发作不是精神障碍。当一个人经历反复且意外的惊恐发作，并因害怕未来发作而持续担忧或出现行为改变，且常常干扰日常生活时，可能被诊断为惊恐障碍。

英文原文：
A panic attack is a one-time or occasional episode of intense fear with physical and emotional symptoms. An isolated panic attack is not a mental disorder.
Panic disorder may be diagnosed when a person experiences recurrent and unexpected panic attacks, along with ongoing worry or behavioral changes due to the fear of future attacks, often interfering with daily life.

metadata.title: 惊恐障碍 / Panic Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 惊恐障碍 惊恐发作 心慌 恐慌
metadata.section: What is the difference between a panic attack and panic disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
惊恐障碍有时在家族中发生，但没有人确切知道为什么有些家庭成员患有它而其他人没有。研究人员发现，大脑的几个部分和某些生物过程可能在恐惧和焦虑中起关键作用。一些研究人员认为惊恐发作就像“虚假警报”，我们身体典型的生存本能要么过于频繁地活跃，要么过于强烈地活跃，或两者的某种组合。例如，患有惊恐障碍的人可能会感到心跳加速，并认为自己心脏病发作。这可能导致恶性循环，使一个人似乎无缘无故地经历惊恐发作，这是惊恐障碍的核心特征。此外，研究人员正在研究压力和環境因素在该障碍中起作用的方式。

英文原文：
Panic disorder sometimes runs in families, but no one knows for sure why some family members have it while others don’t. Researchers have found that several parts of the brain and certain biological processes may play a crucial role in fear and anxiety. Some researchers think panic attacks are like “false alarms,” where our body’s typical survival instincts are active either too often or too strongly, or some combination of the two. For example, someone with panic disorder might feel their heart pounding and assume they’re having a heart attack. This may lead to a vicious cycle, causing a person to experience panic attacks seemingly out of the blue, the central feature of panic disorder. In addition, researchers are looking at the ways stress and environmental factors play a role in the disorder.

metadata.title: 惊恐障碍 / Panic Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 惊恐障碍 惊恐发作 心慌 恐慌
metadata.section: What causes panic disorder? / 影响因素 风险因素

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
要被诊断为惊恐障碍，一个人必须经历反复的、意外的惊恐发作。他们还必须在至少1个月的时间里担心会有更多惊恐发作、对发作的含义感到害怕，或改变自己的行为以试图避免未来的发作。如果你认为自己正在经历惊恐障碍的症状，请与医疗保健提供者交谈，例如初级保健医生、精神科医生、心理学家或临床社会工作者。在就诊期间，提供者可能会询问你的症状何时开始、持续了多长时间、发生频率以及对你生活的影响。在讨论你的病史后，提供者可能会进行体格检查，以确保不是无关的身体问题引起了你的症状。

英文原文：
To be diagnosed with panic disorder, a person must experience recurrent, unexpected panic attacks. They must also spend at least 1 month worrying about having more panic attacks, feeling scared about what the attacks mean, or changing their behavior to try to avoid future attacks.
If you think you’re experiencing symptoms of panic disorder, talk to a health care provider, such as a primary care doctor, psychiatrist, psychologist, or clinical social worker. During the visit, the provider may ask when your symptoms began, how long they have lasted, how often they occur, and their impact on your life. After discussing your history, the provider may conduct a physical exam to ensure that an unrelated physical problem is not causing your symptoms.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
惊恐障碍患者可能同时患有其他精神疾病和躯体疾病或状况，包括抑郁症、其他焦虑障碍、创伤后应激障碍、强迫症、双相障碍、心血管疾病、呼吸系统疾病、肠易激综合征或甲状腺问题。惊恐障碍也常与酒精和物质滥用相关。广场恐惧症有时可作为惊恐障碍的共病出现。广场恐惧症患者对某些场所或情境有强烈的恐惧或焦虑，在这些场所或情境中，如果他们出现惊恐发作或类似惊恐的症状，可能难以逃离或无法获得帮助。了解更多关于广场恐惧症的信息。多种障碍并存会使治疗更加复杂，同时患有惊恐障碍和共病精神障碍的人可能受益于一个全面的治疗计划，以解决其心理健康的各个方面。

英文原文：
Some people with panic disorder have other mental and physical health disorders or conditions, including depression, other anxiety disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, bipolar disorder, cardiovascular disease, respiratory disorders, irritable bowel syndrome, or thyroid problems. Panic disorder is also commonly associated with alcohol and substance misuse.
Agoraphobia can sometimes develop as a co-occurring condition of panic disorder. People with agoraphobia have an intense fear or anxiety of certain places or situations where escape or obtaining help might be difficult or unavailable if they were to experience a panic attack or panic-like symptoms. Learn more about agoraphobia .
The presence of multiple disorders can make treatment more complex, and people with panic disorder and co-occurring mental disorders may benefit from a comprehensive treatment plan that addresses all aspects of their mental health.

惊恐障碍的治疗通常包括心理治疗、药物治疗或两者兼有。选择正确的治疗方案基于个人的需求、偏好和医疗状况，以及与心理健康专业人员或医疗保健提供者的咨询。找到最佳治疗可能需要反复尝试，且心理治疗和药物治疗都需要一些时间才能起效。

英文原文：
Treatment for panic disorder typically involves psychotherapy, medication, or both. Choosing the right treatment plan is based on a person’s needs, preferences, and medical situation, as well as consultation with a mental health professional or a health care provider. Finding the best treatment may take trial and error, and both psychotherapy and medication can take some time to work.

metadata.section: How is panic disorder treated? / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
心理治疗（也称为谈话治疗或咨询）当面进行或通过远程医疗虚拟进行均可有效。提供者可能使用数字或移动技术（如应用程序或其他工具）来支持或补充治疗。不同的疗法适用于不同类型的人。认知行为疗法（CBT）是一种有研究支持的心理治疗方法，常用于治疗惊恐障碍。CBT教会一个人以不同的方式思考、行为和应对惊恐发作期间或之前发生的感受。一旦一个人学会对惊恐发作期间焦虑和恐惧的身体感觉做出不同的反应，发作的频率就会降低。CBT已得到充分研究，是心理治疗的“金标准”选择。暴露疗法是一种常见的CBT方法，侧重于面对与惊恐障碍症状相关的恐惧和信念，以帮助一个人参与他们一直回避的活动。内感受暴露是一种CBT技术，涉及暴露于与惊恐发作和惊恐障碍症状相关的身体感觉。暴露疗法可与放松练习和呼吸训练技术一起使用。了解更多关于心理治疗的信息。

英文原文：
Psychotherapy (also called talk therapy or counseling) can be effective when delivered in person or virtually via telehealth. A provider may support or supplement therapy using digital or mobile technology, like apps or other tools. Different therapies work for different types of people.
Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), a research-supported type of psychotherapy, is commonly used to treat panic disorder. CBT teaches a person different ways of thinking, behaving, and reacting to the feelings that happen during or before a panic attack. The attacks can become less frequent once a person learns to react differently to the physical sensations of anxiety and fear during a panic attack. CBT has been well studied and is the “gold standard” choice for psychotherapy.
Exposure therapy is a common CBT method that focuses on confronting the fears and beliefs associated with panic disorder symptoms to help a person engage in activities they have been avoiding. Interoceptive exposure is a CBT technique that involves exposure to bodily sensations associated with panic attacks and panic disorder symptoms. Exposure therapy may be used along with relaxation exercises and breathing training techniques.
Learn more about psychotherapy .

Practicing a healthy lifestyle can also help combat panic disorder, although this alone cannot replace treatment. Make sure to get enough sleep and exercise, eat a healthy diet, and turn to family and friends you trust for support. Learn more ways to take care of your mental health .

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
社交焦虑障碍是一种常见的焦虑障碍。社交焦虑障碍患者在可能被他人审视、评价或评判的情境中会感到焦虑或恐惧的症状，例如公开演讲、结识新朋友、约会、参加求职面试、在课堂上回答问题、寻求帮助，或不得不与商店收银员交谈。做日常事情，例如在他人面前吃喝或使用公共卫生间，也可能因担心被羞辱、评判或拒绝而引起焦虑或恐惧。这种恐惧通常感觉无法控制，并可能干扰日常生活。社交焦虑障碍患者可能在社交情境发生前数周就担心参与其中。有时，他们最终会回避引起痛苦或产生尴尬感的地方或活动。在某些情况下，焦虑可能仅在表现性情境中出现，例如发表演讲、参加体育比赛或在舞台上演奏乐器。社交焦虑障碍通常始于童年或青春期，可能类似于极度害羞或回避公共场合或社交互动。女性比男性更常见，这种差异在青少年和年轻成人中更为明显。通过正确的治疗和支持，社交焦虑障碍患者可以管理他们的焦虑并改善生活质量。

英文原文：
Social anxiety disorder is a common type of anxiety disorder. A person with social anxiety disorder feels symptoms of anxiety or fear in situations where they may be scrutinized, evaluated, or judged by others, such as speaking in public, meeting new people, dating, being on a job interview, answering a question in class, asking for help, or having to talk to a cashier in a store. Doing everyday things, such as eating or drinking in front of others or using a public restroom, may also cause anxiety or fear due to concerns about being humiliated, judged, or rejected.
This fear often feels uncontrollable and can interfere with daily life. People with social anxiety disorder may worry about engaging in social situations for weeks before they happen. Sometimes, they end up avoiding places or events that cause distress or generate feelings of embarrassment. In some cases, anxiety may arise only during performance situations such as giving a speech, competing in a sports game, or playing a musical instrument on stage.
Social anxiety disorder usually starts during childhood or adolescence and may resemble extreme shyness or avoidance of public situations or social interactions. It occurs more frequently in women than in men, and this difference is more pronounced in adolescents and young adults. With the right treatment and support, people with social anxiety disorder can manage their anxiety and improve their quality of life.

metadata.title: 社交焦虑 / Social Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 社交焦虑 被评价 害怕社交 演讲紧张
metadata.section: What is social anxiety disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
当不得不在他人面前表现或身处他人之中时，社交焦虑障碍患者可能会：脸红、出汗或颤抖；心跳加快；感到“大脑一片空白”，或感到恶心；身体姿势僵硬，或说话声音过于轻柔；难以进行眼神接触，难以待在陌生人身旁，或在社交场合与人交谈，即使他们想这样做；感到难为情，或害怕别人会对自己作出负面评价；回避有他人在场的场所或可能需要与他人互动的情境；分析自己的表现，并找出自己在互动中自认为的缺陷；预期负面社交情境会带来最糟糕的后果。患有社交焦虑障碍的儿童和青少年可能会经历与成人相似的症状，但也可能会：试图逃避上学；难以交朋友；主诉胃痛或头痛；在社交场合情绪爆发；拒绝在社交场合说话或参与。对于所有社交焦虑障碍患者，症状可能会随时间波动，并且在重大压力或变化时期往往更严重。回避引发焦虑的情境在短期内可能感觉有帮助，但如果不治疗，焦虑很可能会持续存在。

英文原文：
When having to perform in front of or be around others, people with social anxiety disorder may:
Blush, sweat, or tremble
Have a rapid heart rate
Feel their “mind going blank,” or feel sick to their stomach
Have a rigid body posture or speak with an overly soft voice
Find it difficult to make eye contact, be around people they don’t know, or talk to people in social situations, even when they want to
Feel self-consciousness or fear that people will judge them negatively
Avoid places where there are other people or situations where they may have to interact with others
Analyze their performance and identify self-perceived flaws in interactions
Expect the worst possible consequences from a negative social situation
Children and teens with social anxiety disorder may experience similar symptoms to adults, but also may:
Try to avoid going to school
Have difficulty making friends
Complain of stomachaches or headaches
Have emotional outbursts in social situations
Refuse to speak or participate in social situations
For all people with social anxiety disorder, symptoms may fluctuate over time and are often worse during times of significant stress or change. Avoiding situations that cause anxiety may feel helpful in the short term, but the anxiety is likely to remain without treatment.

metadata.section: What are the signs and symptoms of social anxiety disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
社交焦虑障碍可能在家族中遗传，但没有人确切知道为什么有些家庭成员患有此病而另一些没有。研究人员发现，大脑的多个部分参与恐惧和焦虑，遗传影响这些脑区的功能。此外，研究人员正在研究压力和環境因素在该障碍中所起的作用。

英文原文：
Social anxiety disorder may run in families, but no one knows for sure why some family members have it while others don’t. Researchers have found that several parts of the brain are involved in fear and anxiety, and genetics influences how these brain areas function. In addition, researchers are looking at the role that stress and environmental factors play in the disorder.

metadata.section: What causes social anxiety disorder? / 影响因素 风险因素

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
要被诊断为社交焦虑障碍，一个人必须对可能被他人评判或审视的社交情境有强烈的恐惧或焦虑。他们可能会试图回避这些情境，或在面对这些情境时感到极度不适。这些感受必须持续至少6个月，并干扰日常生活，如工作、学习或人际关系。如果你认为自己正在经历社交焦虑障碍的症状，请与医疗保健提供者交谈，例如初级保健医生、精神科医生、心理学家或临床社会工作者。在就诊期间，提供者可能会询问你的症状何时开始、持续了多长时间、出现的频率以及对你生活的影响。在讨论你的病史后，提供者可能会进行体格检查，以确保不是无关的身体问题导致你的症状。

英文原文：
To be diagnosed with social anxiety disorder, a person must have strong fear or anxiety about social situations where they might be judged or scrutinized by others. They may try to avoid these situations or face them with extreme discomfort. These feelings must last at least 6 months and interfere with daily life, such as work, school, or relationships.
If you think you’re experiencing symptoms of social anxiety disorder, talk to a health care provider, such as a primary care doctor, psychiatrist, psychologist, or clinical social worker. During the visit, the provider may ask when your symptoms began, how long they have lasted, how often they occur, and their impact on your life. After discussing your history, the provider may conduct a physical exam to ensure that an unrelated physical problem is not causing your symptoms.

documents.content:

社交焦虑障碍患者中，有些人还患有其他精神或躯体健康障碍或状况，包括抑郁症、其他焦虑障碍、强迫症、注意缺陷/多动障碍（ADHD）、躯体变形障碍或双相障碍。社交焦虑障碍也常与酒精和物质滥用相关。社交焦虑障碍患者不太可能向医疗保健提供者寻求诊断或治疗。提供者通常在治疗患者共存的状况时识别出该障碍。多种障碍并存可能使治疗更为复杂，同时患有社交焦虑障碍和共病精神障碍的人可能受益于一个全面的治疗计划，以应对其心理健康的各个方面。

英文原文：
Some people with social anxiety disorder have other mental and physical health disorders or conditions, including depression, other anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), body dysmorphic disorder, or bipolar disorder. Social anxiety disorder is also commonly associated with alcohol and substance misuse.
People with social anxiety disorder are less likely to seek help from a health care provider for diagnosis or treatment. Providers often identify the disorder when treating a person for a co-existing condition.
The presence of multiple disorders can make treatment more complex, and people with social anxiety disorder and co-occurring mental disorders may benefit from a comprehensive treatment plan that addresses all aspects of their mental health.

metadata.title: 社交焦虑 / Social Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
metadata.keywords: 社交焦虑 被评价 害怕社交 演讲紧张
metadata.section: How is social anxiety disorder treated? / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
心理治疗（也称为谈话治疗或咨询）当面进行或通过远程医疗虚拟进行均可有效。提供者可能使用数字或移动技术（如应用程序或其他工具）来支持或补充治疗。不同的疗法适用于不同类型的人。认知行为疗法（CBT）是一种有研究支持的心理治疗类型，常用于治疗社交焦虑障碍。CBT教给一个人不同的思考、行为和应对情境的方式，以帮助他们减少焦虑和恐惧。CBT还可以帮助一个人学习和练习社交技能，这对治疗社交焦虑障碍非常重要。CBT已得到充分研究，是心理治疗的“金标准”选择。暴露疗法是一种CBT方法，侧重于逐步面对焦虑障碍背后的恐惧，以帮助一个人参与他们一直回避的活动。暴露疗法可与放松练习一起使用。以团体治疗形式提供的CBT也可以为社交焦虑障碍提供独特益处。社交焦虑障碍的另一种治疗选择是接纳与承诺疗法（ACT）。ACT采用与CBT不同的方法，鼓励对想法和行为进行非评判性接纳，并促进参与有意义的活动。ACT使用正念和目标设定等策略来减少一个人的不适和焦虑。越来越多的研究证明其对治疗社交焦虑障碍的有效性。了解更多关于心理治疗的信息。

英文原文：
Psychotherapy (also called talk therapy or counseling) can be effective when delivered in person or virtually via telehealth. A provider may support or supplement therapy using digital or mobile technology, like apps or other tools. Different therapies work for different types of people.
Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), a research-supported type of psychotherapy, is commonly used to treat social anxiety disorder. CBT teaches a person different ways of thinking, behaving, and reacting to situations to help them feel less anxious and fearful. CBT also can help a person learn and practice social skills, which is very important for treating social anxiety disorder. CBT has been well studied and is the “gold standard” choice for psychotherapy.
Exposure therapy is a CBT method that focuses on progressively confronting the fears underlying an anxiety disorder to help a person engage in activities they have been avoiding. Exposure therapy may be used along with relaxation exercises. CBT delivered in a group therapy format also can offer unique benefits for social anxiety disorder.
Another treatment option for social anxiety disorder is acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT). ACT takes a different approach than CBT, encouraging nonjudgmental acceptance of thoughts and behaviors and promoting engagement in meaningful activities. ACT uses strategies such as mindfulness and goal setting to reduce a person’s discomfort and anxiety. There is a growing body of research demonstrating its effectiveness for treating social anxiety disorder.
Learn more about psychotherapy .

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
有些社交焦虑的人觉得支持小组有帮助。在一群都患有社交焦虑障碍的人当中，一个人可以获得关于他人如何看待自己的无偏见、诚实的反馈。这让他们了解到，自己关于被评判和拒绝的想法可能并不真实，或者是扭曲的。一个人还可以了解到其他社交焦虑障碍患者如何应对并克服对社交情境的恐惧。支持小组有线下和线上两种形式。然而，你从支持小组成员那里得到的任何建议都应谨慎使用，并且不能替代医疗保健提供者的治疗建议。

英文原文：
Some people with social anxiety find support groups helpful. In a group of people who all have social anxiety disorder, a person can receive unbiased, honest feedback about how others perceive them. This allows them to learn that their thoughts about judgment and rejection may not be true or are distorted. A person can also learn how others with social anxiety disorder approach and overcome the fear of social situations.
Support groups are available both in person and online. However, any advice you receive from a support group member should be used cautiously and does not replace treatment recommendations from a health care provider.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
生活可能充满压力——你可能会因为学业表现、创伤性事件（如大流行病、自然灾害或暴力行为）或生活变化而感到压力。每个人都会时不时感到压力。什么是压力？压力是对外部原因的身体或心理反应，例如有很多作业或患有疾病。压力源可能是一次性或短期的发生，也可能在长时间内反复发生。什么是焦虑？焦虑是身体对压力的反应，即使当前没有威胁也可能发生。如果这种焦虑没有消失并开始干扰你的生活，它可能会影响你的健康。你可能会遇到睡眠问题，或免疫、消化、心血管和生殖系统的问题。你也可能面临更高的风险患上精神疾病，如焦虑障碍或抑郁症。阅读更多关于焦虑障碍的内容。那么，你怎么知道何时寻求帮助？

英文原文：
Life can be stressful—you may feel stressed about performance at school, traumatic events (such as a pandemic, a natural disaster, or an act of violence), or a life change. Everyone feels stress from time to time.
What is stress? Stress is the physical or mental response to an external cause, such as having a lot of homework or having an illness. A stressor may be a one-time or short-term occurrence, or it can happen repeatedly over a long time.
What is anxiety? Anxiety is your body's reaction to stress and can occur even if there is no current threat.
If that anxiety doesn’t go away and begins to interfere with your life, it could affect your health. You could experience problems with sleeping, or with your immune, digestive, cardiovascular, and reproductive systems. You also may be at higher risk for developing a mental illness such as an anxiety disorder or depression. Read more about anxiety disorders .
So, how do you know when to seek help?

documents.content:

压力 / 我压力太大了！情况说明
压力与焦虑
通常是对外部原因的反应，例如参加一场大考或与朋友争吵。一旦情况解决就会消失。可以是积极的，也可以是消极的。例如，它可能激励你赶上截止日期，也可能导致你失眠。过度担忧不安紧张头痛或身体疼痛高血压失眠通常是内在的，意味着它是你对压力的反应。通常涉及一种持续存在的忧虑或恐惧感，这种感受不会消失，并且会干扰你的生活。即使没有迫在眉睫的威胁，它也持续存在。

英文原文：
Generally is a response to an external cause, such as taking a big test or arguing with a friend.
Goes away once the situation is resolved.
Can be positive or negative. For example, it may inspire you to meet a deadline, or it may cause you to lose sleep.
Excessive worry
Uneasiness
Tension
Headaches or body pain
High blood pressure
Loss of sleep
Generally is internal, meaning it's your reaction to stress.
Usually involves a persistent feeling of apprehension or dread that doesn't go away, and that interferes with how you live your life.
Is constant, even if there is no immediate threat.

每个人都会经历压力，有时这种压力可能让人感到不堪重负。如果感觉无法管理压力，并且压力的症状：干扰你的日常生活。导致你回避做事。似乎总是存在。你可能面临焦虑障碍的风险。

Everyone experiences stress, and sometimes that stress can feel overwhelming. You may be at risk for an anxiety disorder if it feels like you can’t manage the stress and if the symptoms of your stress:
Interfere with your everyday life.
Cause you to avoid doing things.

metadata.section: It’s important to manage your stress. / 自我照顾 应对 调节

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
了解是什么导致或触发你的压力，以及哪些应对技巧对你有效，可以帮助减轻你的焦虑并改善你的日常生活。可能需要反复尝试才能发现最适合你的方法。当你开始感到不堪重负时，可以尝试以下一些活动：写日记。下载一个提供放松练习（如深呼吸或可视化）或正念练习技巧的应用程序，正念是一种主动关注当下的心理过程。锻炼，并确保你健康、规律地饮食。坚持睡眠规律，并确保你获得足够的睡眠。避免摄入过量咖啡因，如软饮料或咖啡。识别并挑战你的负面和无益的想法。向你那些以积极方式帮助你应对的朋友或家人寻求支持。

英文原文：
Learning what causes or triggers your stress and what coping techniques work for you can help reduce your anxiety and improve your daily life. It may take trial and error to discover what works best for you. Here are some activities you can try when you start to feel overwhelmed:
Keep a journal.
Download an app that provides relaxation exercises (such as deep breathing or visualization) or tips for practicing mindfulness, which is a psychological process of actively paying attention to the present moment.
Exercise, and make sure you are eating healthy, regular meals.
Stick to a sleep routine, and make sure you are getting enough sleep.
Avoid drinking excess caffeine such as soft drinks or coffee.
Identify and challenge your negative and unhelpful thoughts.
Reach out to your friends or family members who help you cope in a positive way.

如果你难以应对，或者你的压力或焦虑症状持续不消退，可能是时候与专业人士交谈了。心理治疗（也称为谈话治疗）和药物是焦虑的两种主要治疗方法，许多人从两者的结合中获益。如果你或你认识的人患有精神疾病、情绪困扰，或对自己的心理健康有担忧，有办法获得帮助。阅读更多关于获得帮助的信息。

If you are struggling to cope, or the symptoms of your stress or anxiety won’t go away, it may be time to talk to a professional. Psychotherapy (also called talk therapy) and medication are the two main treatments for anxiety, and many people benefit from a combination of the two.
If you or someone you know has a mental illness, is struggling emotionally, or has concerns about their mental health, there are ways to get help. Read more about getting help .
