documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
精神病性症状 / 理解精神病

什么是精神病？/ 定义 含义 什么是

精神病是指一组影响心智的症状，此时与现实已出现某种程度的脱节。在精神病发作期间，一个人的思维和感知受到扰乱，他们可能难以辨别什么是真实的、什么不是。

英文原文：
Psychosis refers to a collection of symptoms that affect the mind, where there has been some loss of contact with reality. During an episode of psychosis, a person’s thoughts and perceptions are disrupted and they may have difficulty recognizing what is real and what is not.

metadata.title: 精神病性症状 / Understanding Psychosis
metadata.keywords: 精神病性症状 幻觉 妄想 精神分裂症
metadata.section: What is psychosis? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
很难知道经历精神病性症状的人数。研究估计，每年每10万人中有15至100人出现精神病性症状。精神病性症状通常始于成年早期，即一个人十几岁晚期到二十多岁中期。然而，人们可能在更年轻和更年长的年龄经历精神病性发作，并且作为许多障碍和疾病的一部分。例如，患有神经系统疾病的老年人可能有更高的精神病性症状风险。

英文原文：
It is difficult to know the number of people who experience psychosis. Studies estimate that between 15 and 100 people out of 100,000 develop psychosis each year.
Psychosis often begins in young adulthood when a person is in their late teens to mid-20s. However, people can experience a psychotic episode at younger and older ages and as a part of many disorders and illnesses. For instance, older adults with neurological disorders may be at higher risk for psychosis.

metadata.title: 精神病性症状 / Understanding Psychosis
metadata.keywords: 精神病性症状 幻觉 妄想 精神分裂症
metadata.section: Who develops psychosis? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
精神病性症状 / 理解精神病

精神病有哪些体征和症状？ / 常见表现 症状 识别

精神病患者通常会出现妄想（错误的信念，例如认为电视上的人在向他们发送特殊信息，或认为他人在试图伤害他们）和幻觉（看到或听到他人看不到或听不到的事物，例如听到声音告诉他们去做某事或批评他们）。其他症状可能包括语无伦次或毫无意义的言语，以及不适合情境的行为。然而，在精神病发展之前，一个人往往会表现出行为上的变化。精神病的警示性行为迹象包括：多疑、偏执想法或与他人相处时感到不安；难以清晰、有逻辑地思考；社交退缩，独处时间大幅增加；不寻常或过度强烈的想法、奇怪的感觉或缺乏感觉；自我照料或个人卫生下降；睡眠紊乱，包括入睡困难和睡眠时间减少；难以区分现实与幻想；言语混乱或沟通困难；成绩或工作表现突然下降。除了这些症状外，精神病患者还可能经历更一般的行为变化，包括：情绪紊乱、焦虑、缺乏动力、整体功能困难。在某些情况下，经历精神病发作的人可能以令人困惑和不可预测的方式行事，并可能伤害自己，或对他人构成威胁或变得暴力。暴力和自杀的风险会随着精神病的治疗而降低，因此寻求帮助很重要。如果你发现自己正在经历这些行为变化，或在朋友或家人身上注意到这些变化，并且它们开始加重或没有消失，请向医疗保健提供者求助。

英文原文：
People with psychosis typically experience delusions (false beliefs, for example, that people on television are sending them special messages or that others are trying to hurt them) and hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that others do not, such as hearing voices telling them to do something or criticizing them). Other symptoms can include incoherent or nonsense speech and behavior that is inappropriate for the situation.
However, a person will often show changes in their behavior before psychosis develops. Behavioral warning signs for psychosis include:
Suspiciousness, paranoid ideas, or uneasiness with others
Trouble thinking clearly and logically
Withdrawing socially and spending a lot more time alone
Unusual or overly intense ideas, strange feelings, or a lack of feelings
Decline in self-care or personal hygiene
Disruption of sleep, including difficulty falling asleep and reduced sleep time
Difficulty telling reality from fantasy
Confused speech or trouble communicating
Sudden drop in grades or job performance
Alongside these symptoms, a person with psychosis may also experience more general changes in behavior that include:
Emotional disruption
Anxiety
Lack of motivation
Difficulty functioning overall
In some cases, a person experiencing a psychotic episode may behave in confusing and unpredictable ways and may harm themselves or become threatening or violent toward others. The risk of violence and suicide decreases with treatment for psychosis, so it is important to seek help. If you find that you are experiencing these changes in behavior or notice them in a friend or family member and they begin to intensify or do not go away, reach out to a health care provider.

metadata.title: 精神病性症状 / Understanding Psychosis
metadata.keywords: 精神病性症状 幻觉 妄想 精神分裂症
metadata.section: What are the signs and symptoms of psychosis? / 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
精神病性症状没有单一病因。精神病性症状似乎是遗传风险、脑发育差异以及暴露于应激源或创伤等复杂因素共同作用的结果。精神病性症状可能是某种精神疾病的症状，如精神分裂症、双相障碍或重度抑郁。然而，一个人可能出现精神病性症状，却从未被诊断为精神分裂症或任何其他疾病。对于老年人，精神病性症状可能是晚年出现的躯体或精神疾病的一部分。精神病性症状也可能是某些老年期疾病的症状，包括帕金森病、阿尔茨海默病及相关痴呆。精神病性症状的其他可能原因包括睡眠剥夺、某些处方药以及酒精或药物滥用。精神分裂症等精神疾病通常通过排除这些其他原因来诊断。合格的精神卫生专业人员（如心理学家、精神科医生或社会工作者）可以提供全面的评估和准确的诊断。查找有助于为就诊做准备并充分利用就诊时间的建议。如需更多资源，包括向您的医疗保健提供者提出的问题，请访问医疗保健研究与质量局。

英文原文：
There is no one cause of psychosis. Psychosis appears to result from a complex combination of genetic risk, differences in brain development, and exposure to stressors or trauma. Psychosis may be a symptom of a mental illness, such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or severe depression. However, a person can experience psychosis and never be diagnosed with schizophrenia or any other disorder.
For older adults, psychosis symptoms can be part of a physical or mental illness that emerges later in life. Psychosis can also be a symptom of some diseases of older age, including Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer’s disease, and related dementias.
Other possible causes of psychosis include sleep deprivation, certain prescription medications, and the misuse of alcohol or drugs. A mental illness, such as schizophrenia, is typically diagnosed by excluding these other causes.
A qualified mental health professional (such as a psychologist, psychiatrist, or social worker) can provide a thorough assessment and accurate diagnosis. Find tips to help prepare for and get the most out of your visit . For additional resources, including questions to ask your health care provider, visit the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality .

metadata.title: 精神病性症状 / Understanding Psychosis
metadata.keywords: 精神病性症状 幻觉 妄想 精神分裂症
metadata.section: What causes psychosis? / 影响因素 风险因素

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
研究表明，一个人在接受治疗前存在精神病性症状超过一年是常见的。缩短这一未治疗精神病持续时间至关重要，因为早期治疗通常意味着更好的康复。合格的心理学家、精神科医生或社会工作者可以做出诊断并帮助制定治疗计划。精神病的治疗通常包括抗精神病药物。有几种不同类型的抗精神病药物，它们有不同的副作用，因此与医疗保健提供者合作确定最有效且副作用最少的药物非常重要。治疗通常还包括其他要素。有大量研究支持协调专科护理，这是一种多要素、以康复为导向的团队方法，用于治疗精神病，促进易于获得护理，并促进专家、经历精神病的人及其家庭成员之间的共同决策。如果人们在精神病性症状出现后尽快开始治疗，他们从协调专科护理中获得的结果会更好。根据《美国精神病学协会精神分裂症患者治疗实践指南》，协调专科护理现在是早期精神病的标准护理。

英文原文：
Studies have shown that it is common for a person to have psychotic symptoms for more than a year before receiving treatment. Reducing this duration of untreated psychosis is critical because early treatment often means better recovery. A qualified psychologist, psychiatrist, or social worker can make a diagnosis and help develop a treatment plan.
Treatment of psychosis usually includes antipsychotic medication. There are several different types of antipsychotic medications, and they have different side effects, so it is important to work with a health care provider to determine the medication that is most effective with the fewest side effects.
Treatment also often includes other elements. There is substantial research support for coordinated specialty care, which is a multi-element, recovery-oriented team approach to treating psychosis that promotes easy access to care and shared decision-making among specialists, the person experiencing psychosis, and family members. People experience better outcomes from coordinated specialty care if they begin treatment as soon as possible after psychotic symptoms emerge.
Coordinated specialty care is now the standard of care for early psychosis, according to “ The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia .”

metadata.title: 精神病性症状 / Understanding Psychosis
metadata.keywords: 精神病性症状 幻觉 妄想 精神分裂症
metadata.section: How is psychosis treated? / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
NIMH不认可特定的精神病性症状诊所，也不评估个体执业者的专业资格或能力。然而，有一些组织可以帮助您在所在地区寻找治疗方案。以下并非所有项目的完整列表，项目出现在列表中并不构成NIMH的认可。早期精神病性症状干预网络（EPINET）：EPINET的早期精神病性症状干预网络诊所向17个州的早期精神病性症状个体提供治疗和服务。全国精神疾病联盟（NAMI）：NAMI帮助热线可以为您联系您所在州的NAMI办公室，并帮助您找到离家较近的项目。此外，您可以在周一至周五东部时间上午10：00至晚上10：00通过以下方式与NAMI帮助热线的人员交谈：致电1-800-950-NAMI（6264）；发送短信“HelpLine”至62640；发送电子邮件至helpline@nami.org。精神病性症状风险与早期精神病性症状项目网络（PEPPNET）：PEPPNET支持早期精神病性症状项目目录，该目录向有精神病性症状风险或经历早期精神病性症状的人提供服务。药物滥用和心理健康服务管理局（SAMHSA）：SAMHSA有一个早期严重精神疾病治疗定位器，用于寻找心理健康治疗设施和项目。

英文原文：
NIMH does not endorse specific psychosis clinics or evaluate individual practitioners’ professional qualifications or competencies. However, several organizations are available to assist in finding a treatment program in your area. The following is not a comprehensive list of all programs, and a program’s inclusion on the list does not constitute an endorsement by NIMH.
Early Psychosis Intervention Network (EPINET) : EPINET’s Early Psychosis Intervention Network Clinics provide treatment and services to individuals with early psychosis across 17 states.
National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) : The NAMI HelpLine can connect you with the NAMI office in your state and help you find programs close to home. Also, you can talk with someone at the NAMI HelpLine, Monday–Friday, 10:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. ET, by: Calling 1-800-950-NAMI (6264) Texting “HelpLine” to 62640 Emailing helpline@nami.org
Psychosis-Risk and Early Psychosis Program Network (PEPPNET) : PEPPNET supports an Early Psychosis Program Directory that provides services to people at risk for or experiencing early psychosis.
Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) : SAMHSA has an Early Serious Mental Illness Treatment Locator for finding mental health treatment facilities and programs.

metadata.title: 精神病性症状 / Understanding Psychosis
metadata.keywords: 精神病性症状 幻觉 妄想 精神分裂症
metadata.section: How can I find help? / 求助 支持 咨询师

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
儿童和青少年在经历或目睹创伤事件（如自然灾害、暴力行为或严重事故）后出现一系列反应是典型的。无论年龄大小，儿童和青少年都可能：报告身体问题，如胃痛或头痛。做噩梦或其他睡眠问题，包括拒绝上床睡觉。注意力难以集中。对通常喜欢的活动失去兴趣。因未能阻止受伤或死亡而感到内疚。有报复的念头。幼儿（5岁及以下）可能：粘着照料者，和/或哭泣、流泪。发脾气，或易怒或捣乱。突然恢复某些行为，如尿床和吮手指。表现出更多的恐惧（例如，害怕黑暗、怪物或独处）。将创伤事件的某些方面融入想象性游戏。年龄较大的儿童（6岁及以上）和青少年可能：在学校出现问题。退缩或与家人和朋友隔离。回避事件的提醒物。使用毒品、酒精或烟草。捣乱、不尊重他人或具有破坏性。愤怒或怨恨。这些反应中许多是正常的，会随时间减轻。如果这些症状持续超过一个月，家庭应联系医疗保健提供者。

英文原文：
It is typical for children and adolescents to have a range of reactions after experiencing or witnessing a traumatic event, such as a natural disaster, an act of violence, or a serious accident.
Regardless of age, children and adolescents may:
Report having physical problems such as stomachaches or headaches.
Have nightmares or other sleep problems, including refusing to go to bed.
Have trouble concentrating.
Lose interest in activities they normally enjoy.
Have feelings of guilt for not preventing injuries or deaths.
Have thoughts of revenge.
Young children (age 5 and younger) may:
Cling to caregivers and/or cry and be tearful.
Have tantrums, or be irritable or disruptive.
Suddenly return to behaviors such as bed-wetting and thumb-sucking.
Show increased fearfulness (for example, fear of the dark, monsters, or being alone).
Incorporate aspects of the traumatic event into imaginary play.
Older children (age 6 and older) and adolescents may:
Have problems in school.
Withdraw or become isolated from family and friends.
Avoid reminders of the event.
Use drugs, alcohol, or tobacco.
Be disruptive, disrespectful, or destructive.
Be angry or resentful.
Many of these reactions are normal and will lessen with time. If these symptoms last for more than a month, the family should reach out to a health care provider.

metadata.title: 应对创伤事件 / Helping Children and Adolescents Cope With Traumatic Events
metadata.keywords: 应对创伤事件 灾难 恢复 陪伴
metadata.section: How do children and adolescents respond to traumatic events? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
成年人如何应对创伤，会极大影响儿童和青少年对创伤的反应。当照护者和家庭成员采取措施支持自身的应对能力时，他们就能更好地照顾他人。照护者和家庭成员可以通过营造安全和支持性的环境、尽可能保持冷静以及减少压力源来提供帮助。儿童和青少年需要知道他们的家人爱他们，并会尽力照顾他们。要：确保儿童和青少年安全，并满足他们的基本需求。允许他们悲伤或哭泣。让他们谈论、书写或画出关于事件及他们的感受。限制他们接触关于创伤事件的重复新闻报道。如果他们睡眠有困难，让他们短期睡在你的房间，或开着灯睡觉。尽量保持日常惯例，如读睡前故事、一起吃晚餐和玩游戏。通过让他们为自己做一些决定来帮助他们感到有掌控感，例如选择餐食或挑选衣服。注意行为、言语、语言使用或强烈情绪的突然变化。如果出现新问题，请联系医疗保健提供者，特别是如果以下任何症状持续超过几周：出现闪回（重新经历事件）心跳加速和出汗容易受惊情感麻木非常悲伤或抑郁。不要：期望儿童和青少年勇敢或坚强。在他们准备好之前让他们讨论事件。如果他们表现出强烈情绪就生气。如果他们开始尿床、行为失控或吮拇指就心烦。做出你无法兑现的承诺（如“你明天就会好起来”或“你很快就能回家。”）

英文原文：
How adults respond to trauma can strongly influence how children and adolescents react to trauma. When caregivers and family members take steps to support their own ability to cope, they can provide better care for others.
Caregivers and family members can help by creating a safe and supportive environment, remaining as calm as possible, and reducing stressors. Children and adolescents need to know that their family members love them and will do their best to take care of them.
Do:
Ensure children and adolescents are safe and that their basic needs are addressed.
Allow them to be sad or cry.
Let them talk, write, or draw pictures about the event and their feelings.
Limit their exposure to repetitive news reports about traumatic events.
Let them sleep in your room (for a short time) or sleep with a light on if they are having trouble sleeping.
Try to stick to routines, such as reading bedtime stories, eating dinner together, and playing games.
Help them feel in control by letting them make some decisions for themselves, such as choosing their meals or picking out their clothes.
Pay attention to sudden changes in behaviors, speech, language use, or strong emotions.
Contact a health care provider if new problems develop, particularly if any of the following symptoms occur for more than a few weeks: Having flashbacks (reliving the event) Having a racing heart and sweating Being easily startled Being emotionally numb Being very sad or depressed
Don’t:
Expect children and adolescents to be brave or tough.
Make them discuss the event before they are ready.
Get angry if they show strong emotions.
Get upset if they begin bed-wetting, acting out, or thumb-sucking.
Make promises you can’t keep (such as “You will be OK tomorrow” or “You will go home soon.”)

metadata.title: 应对创伤事件 / Helping Children and Adolescents Cope With Traumatic Events
metadata.keywords: 应对创伤事件 灾难 恢复 陪伴
metadata.section: What can adults do to help? / 求助 支持 咨询师

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
在创伤性情境期间和之后感到害怕是自然的。恐惧是身体“战斗或逃跑”反应的一部分，这种反应帮助我们避免或应对潜在危险。人们在创伤后可能会经历一系列反应，大多数人会随着时间推移从症状中恢复。那些持续经历症状的人可能会被诊断为创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。

英文原文：
It is natural to feel afraid during and after a traumatic situation. Fear is a part of the body’s “fight-or-flight” response, which helps us avoid or respond to potential danger. People may experience a range of reactions after trauma, and most will recover from their symptoms over time. Those who continue to experience symptoms may be diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: What is post-traumatic stress disorder, or PTSD? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
任何人都可能在任何年龄患上创伤后应激障碍。这包括参战老兵，以及经历过或目睹过身体或性侵犯、虐待、事故、灾难、恐怖袭击或其他严重事件的人。患有创伤后应激障碍的人可能会感到紧张或恐惧，即使他们已不再处于危险之中。并非所有患有创伤后应激障碍的人都经历过危险事件。有时，得知亲属或密友经历了创伤也可能导致创伤后应激障碍。根据美国退伍军人事务部项目国家创伤后应激障碍中心的数据，每100人中约有6人会在其一生中的某个时候经历创伤后应激障碍。女性比男性更可能患上创伤后应激障碍。创伤事件的某些方面和生物学因素（如基因）可能使一些人更可能患上创伤后应激障碍。

英文原文：
Anyone can develop PTSD at any age. This includes combat veterans and people who have experienced or witnessed a physical or sexual assault, abuse, an accident, a disaster, a terror attack, or other serious events. People who have PTSD may feel stressed or frightened, even when they are no longer in danger.
Not everyone with PTSD has been through a dangerous event. Sometimes, learning that a relative or close friend experienced trauma can cause PTSD.
About 6 of every 100 people will experience PTSD at some point in their lifetime, according to the National Center for PTSD, a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs program. Women are more likely than men to develop PTSD. Certain aspects of the traumatic event and biological factors (such as genes) may make some people more likely to develop PTSD.

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: Who develops PTSD? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
创伤后应激障碍的症状通常在创伤事件后3个月内开始出现，但有时也会更晚出现。要符合创伤后应激障碍的诊断标准，一个人的症状必须持续超过1个月，并且症状必须严重到干扰日常生活的各个方面，例如人际关系或工作。这些症状还必须与药物、物质使用或其他疾病无关。该障碍的病程各不相同。尽管有些人在6个月内康复，但另一些人的症状会持续1年或更长时间。创伤后应激障碍患者常伴有共病，例如抑郁、物质使用或一种或多种焦虑障碍。在经历危险事件后，出现一些症状是自然的。例如，有些人可能会感到与经历疏离，仿佛他们是在以局外人身份观察事物，而不是在体验它们。心理健康专业人员——例如精神科医生、心理学家或临床社会工作者——可以判断症状是否符合创伤后应激障碍的诊断标准。要被诊断为创伤后应激障碍，成年人必须至少1个月内具备以下所有情况：至少一种再体验症状至少一种回避症状至少两种唤醒和反应性症状至少两种认知和情绪症状

英文原文：
Symptoms of PTSD usually begin within 3 months of the traumatic event, but they sometimes emerge later. To meet the criteria for PTSD, a person must have symptoms for longer than 1 month, and the symptoms must be severe enough to interfere with aspects of daily life, such as relationships or work. The symptoms also must be unrelated to medication, substance use, or other illness.
The course of the disorder varies. Although some people recover within 6 months, others have symptoms that last for 1 year or longer. People with PTSD often have co-occurring conditions, such as depression, substance use, or one or more anxiety disorders.
After a dangerous event, it is natural to have some symptoms. For example, some people may feel detached from the experience, as though they are observing things as an outsider rather than experiencing them. A mental health professional—such as a psychiatrist, psychologist, or clinical social worker—can determine whether symptoms meet the criteria for PTSD.
To be diagnosed with PTSD, an adult must have all of the following for at least 1 month:
At least one re-experiencing symptom
At least one avoidance symptom
At least two arousal and reactivity symptoms
At least two cognition and mood symptoms

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: What are the symptoms of PTSD? / 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
闪回——重新体验创伤事件，包括身体症状，如心跳加速或出汗；与事件相关的反复出现的记忆或梦境；令人痛苦的想法；压力的身体迹象；想法和感受可以触发这些症状，言语、物体或让人想起该事件的情境也可以触发。

英文原文：
Flashbacks—reliving the traumatic event, including physical symptoms, such as a racing heart or sweating
Recurring memories or dreams related to the event
Distressing thoughts
Physical signs of stress
Thoughts and feelings can trigger these symptoms, as can words, objects, or situations that are reminders of the event.

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: Re-experiencing symptoms / 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
远离那些会让人想起该经历的地点、事件或物品；回避与创伤事件相关的想法或感受。回避症状可能导致人们改变日常习惯。例如，有些人在经历严重车祸后可能会避免开车或乘车。

英文原文：
Staying away from places, events, or objects that are reminders of the experience
Avoiding thoughts or feelings related to the traumatic event
Avoidance symptoms may cause people to change their routines. For example, some people may avoid driving or riding in a car after a serious car accident.

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: Avoidance symptoms / 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
容易被惊吓感到紧张、警觉或坐立不安难以集中注意力难以入睡或保持睡眠感到易怒，并有愤怒或攻击性爆发从事冒险、鲁莽或破坏性行为警觉症状通常是持续存在的。它们可能导致压力和愤怒感，并可能干扰日常生活的部分方面，例如睡眠、进食或集中注意力。

英文原文：
Being easily startled
Feeling tense, on guard, or on edge
Having difficulty concentrating
Having difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep
Feeling irritable and having angry or aggressive outbursts
Engaging in risky, reckless, or destructive behavior
Arousal symptoms are often constant. They can lead to feelings of stress and anger and may interfere with parts of daily life, such as sleeping, eating, or concentrating.

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: Arousal and reactivity symptoms / 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
难以记住创伤事件的关键特征；对自己或世界持负面想法；对自己或他人有过度的责备感；持续的负面情绪，如恐惧、愤怒、内疚或羞耻；对以前的活动失去兴趣；感到与社会隔离；难以感受到积极情绪，如快乐或满足。认知和情绪症状可能在创伤事件后开始或加重。它们可能导致人们感到与朋友或家人疏离。

英文原文：
Trouble remembering key features of the traumatic event
Negative thoughts about oneself or the world
Exaggerated feelings of blame directed toward oneself or others
Ongoing negative emotions, such as fear, anger, guilt, or shame
Loss of interest in previous activities
Feelings of social isolation
Difficulty feeling positive emotions, such as happiness or satisfaction
Cognition and mood symptoms can begin or worsen after the traumatic event. They can lead people to feel detached from friends or family members.

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: Cognition and mood symptoms / 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
儿童和青少年对创伤性事件可能有极端反应，但他们的症状可能与成人不同。在6岁以下的儿童中，症状可能包括：已学会使用厕所后仍尿床；忘记如何说话或无法说话；在游戏时间中重演可怕事件；对父母或其他成人异常粘人。年龄较大的儿童和青少年通常表现出与成人更相似的症状。他们还可能出现破坏性、不尊重或毁灭性行为。年龄较大的儿童和青少年可能因未能防止伤害或死亡而感到内疚，或产生报复的想法。查找更多关于帮助儿童和青少年应对创伤性事件的信息。

英文原文：
Children and teens can have extreme reactions to traumatic events, but their symptoms may not be the same as those seen in adults. In children younger than age 6, symptoms can include:
Wetting the bed after having learned to use the toilet
Forgetting how to talk or being unable to talk
Acting out the scary event during playtime
Being unusually clingy with a parent or other adult
Older children and teens usually show symptoms more like those seen in adults. They also may develop disruptive, disrespectful, or destructive behaviors. Older children and teens may feel guilt over not preventing injury or death, or have thoughts of revenge.
Find more information on helping children and adolescents cope with traumatic events .

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: How do children and teens react to trauma? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
为什么有些人会患上创伤后应激障碍，而有些人不会？
并非每个经历过危险事件的人都会患上创伤后应激障碍——许多因素在起作用。其中一些因素在创伤之前就已存在；另一些则在创伤事件期间和之后发挥作用。可能增加患上创伤后应激障碍可能性的风险因素包括：既往经历过创伤，尤其是童年时期；受伤或目睹他人受伤或死亡；感到恐惧、无助或极度害怕；事件后几乎没有或完全没有社会支持；事件后应对压力源，如失去亲人、疼痛和受伤，或失去工作或住所；有精神疾病或物质使用的个人史或家族史。可能降低患上创伤后应激障碍可能性的韧性因素包括：寻求并接受来自朋友、家人或支持团体的支持；学会接纳自己对创伤事件的反应；拥有应对策略以度过创伤事件并从中学习；在感到恐惧的同时，做好准备并能够在令人不安的事件发生时做出应对。

英文原文：
Not everyone who lives through a dangerous event develops PTSD—many factors play a part. Some of these factors are present before the trauma; others play a role during and after a traumatic event.
Risk factors that may increase the likelihood of developing PTSD include:
Exposure to previous traumatic experiences, particularly during childhood
Getting hurt or seeing people hurt or killed
Feeling horror, helplessness, or extreme fear
Having little or no social support after the event
Dealing with stressors after the event, such as the loss of a loved one, pain and injury, or loss of a job or home
Having a personal history or family history of mental illness or substance use
Resilience factors that may reduce the likelihood of developing PTSD include:
Seeking out and receiving support from friends, family, or support groups
Learning to feel okay with one’s actions in response to a traumatic event
Having a coping strategy for getting through and learning from a traumatic event
Being prepared and able to respond to upsetting events as they occur, despite feeling fear

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: Why do some people develop PTSD and other people do not? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
有创伤后应激障碍症状的人与有治疗创伤后应激障碍经验的心理健康专业人员合作非常重要。主要治疗方法是心理治疗、药物治疗，或心理治疗与药物治疗相结合。有经验的心理健康专业人员可以帮助人们为其症状和需求找到最佳治疗方案。一些有创伤后应激障碍的人，例如处于虐待关系中的人，可能正经历持续创伤。在这些情况下，当治疗同时针对创伤情境和创伤后应激障碍症状时，通常最为有效。经历创伤事件或患有创伤后应激障碍的人也可能出现惊恐障碍、抑郁、物质使用或自杀念头。针对这些状况的治疗有助于创伤后的康复。研究表明，来自家人和朋友的支持也可以是康复的重要组成部分。查找有助于你准备并指导你与医疗保健提供者谈论心理健康的提示。

英文原文：
It is important for people with PTSD symptoms to work with a mental health professional who has experience treating PTSD. The main treatments are psychotherapy, medications, or a combination of psychotherapy and medications. An experienced mental health professional can help people find the best treatment plan for their symptoms and needs.
Some people with PTSD, such as those in abusive relationships, may be living through ongoing trauma. In these cases, treatment is usually most effective when it addresses both the traumatic situation and the symptoms of PTSD. People who experience traumatic events or who have PTSD may also experience panic disorder, depression, substance use, or suicidal thoughts. Treatment for these conditions can help with recovery after trauma. Research shows that support from family and friends also can be an essential part of recovery.
Find tips to help prepare and guide you in talking to your health care provider about your mental health .

metadata.title: 创伤后应激障碍 / Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
metadata.keywords: 创伤后应激障碍 PTSD 创伤 闪回
metadata.section: How is PTSD treated? / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
心理治疗，有时称为谈话治疗，包括心理健康专业人员用来帮助人们识别和改变令人困扰的情绪、想法和行为的一系列治疗技术。心理治疗可以为创伤后应激障碍患者及其家人提供支持、教育和指导。治疗可以一对一进行，也可以在团体环境中进行，通常持续6至12周，但可能持续更长时间。某些类型的心理治疗针对创伤后应激障碍症状，而其他类型则侧重于社会、家庭或工作相关问题。有效的心理治疗通常强调几个关键组成部分，包括学习帮助识别触发因素和管理症状的技能。一种常见的心理治疗类型称为认知行为疗法，可以包括暴露疗法和认知重构。暴露疗法帮助人们学会管理恐惧，方法是以安全的方式逐渐让他们暴露于所经历的创伤。作为暴露疗法的一部分，人们可能会思考或写下创伤，或访问事件发生的地点。这种疗法可以帮助创伤后应激障碍患者减少引起他们痛苦症状。认知重构帮助人们理解创伤事件。有时人们记住事件的方式与事件发生的方式不同，或者他们可能对不是他们过错的事情感到内疚或羞耻。认知重构可以帮助创伤后应激障碍患者以现实的方式思考所发生的事情。了解更多关于心理治疗的信息。

英文原文：
Psychotherapy, sometimes called talk therapy, includes a variety of treatment techniques that mental health professionals use to help people identify and change troubling emotions, thoughts, and behaviors. Psychotherapy can provide support, education, and guidance to people with PTSD and their families. Treatment can take place one on one or in a group setting and usually lasts 6 to 12 weeks but can last longer.
Some types of psychotherapy target PTSD symptoms, while others focus on social, family, or job-related problems. Effective psychotherapies often emphasize a few key components, including learning skills to help identify triggers and manage symptoms.
A common type of psychotherapy called cognitive behavioral therapy can include exposure therapy and cognitive restructuring.
Exposure therapy helps people learn to manage their fear by gradually exposing them, in a safe way, to the trauma they experienced. As part of exposure therapy, people may think or write about the trauma or visit the place where it happened. This therapy can help people with PTSD reduce symptoms that cause them distress.
Cognitive restructuring helps people make sense of the traumatic event. Sometimes people remember the event differently from how it happened, or they may feel guilt or shame about something that is not their fault. Cognitive restructuring can help people with PTSD think about what happened in a realistic way.
Learn more about psychotherapy .

documents.content:

通过治疗，你可以好转。以下是一些你可以为自己做的事情：与你的医疗保健提供者讨论治疗方案，并遵循你的治疗计划。进行锻炼、正念或其他有助于减轻压力的活动。尽量保持用餐、锻炼和睡眠的规律。设定切合实际的目标，专注于你能应对的事情。花时间与可信赖的朋友或亲属相处，并告诉他们可能触发症状的事情。预期你的症状会逐渐改善，而不是立即改善。避免使用酒精或药物。

英文原文：
You can get better with treatment. Here are some things you can do to help yourself:
Talk with your health care provider about treatment options and follow your treatment plan.
Engage in exercise, mindfulness, or other activities that help reduce stress.
Try to maintain routines for meals, exercise, and sleep.
Set realistic goals and focus on what you can manage.
Spend time with trusted friends or relatives and tell them about things that may trigger symptoms.
Expect your symptoms to improve gradually, not immediately.
Avoid the use of alcohol or drugs.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
如果你认识可能正在经历创伤后应激障碍的人，你能做的最重要的事情就是帮助那个人获得正确的诊断和治疗。有些人可能需要帮助才能与他们的医疗保健提供者预约；另一些人则可能受益于有人陪同他们去医疗保健就诊。如果一位亲密的朋友或亲属被诊断为创伤后应激障碍，你可以鼓励他们遵循他们的治疗计划。如果他们的症状在6到8周后没有改善，你可以鼓励他们与他们的医疗保健提供者谈论此事。你也可以：提供情感支持、理解、耐心和鼓励。了解创伤后应激障碍，以便你能理解你的朋友正在经历什么。仔细倾听。注意这个人的感受以及可能触发创伤后应激障碍症状的情境。分享积极的分散注意力的活动，例如散步、外出和其他活动。

英文原文：
If you know someone who may be experiencing PTSD, the most important thing you can do is to help that person get the right diagnosis and treatment. Some people may need help making an appointment with their health care provider; others may benefit from having someone accompany them to their health care visits.
If a close friend or relative is diagnosed with PTSD, you can encourage them to follow their treatment plan. If their symptoms do not improve after 6 to 8 weeks, you can encourage them to talk about it with their health care provider. You also can:
Offer emotional support, understanding, patience, and encouragement.
Learn about PTSD so you can understand what your friend is experiencing.
Listen carefully. Pay attention to the person’s feelings and the situations that may trigger PTSD symptoms.
Share positive distractions, such as walks, outings, and other activities.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
每个人有时都会感到悲伤或情绪低落，但这些感觉通常会过去。抑郁（也称为重性抑郁、重性抑郁障碍或临床抑郁）则不同。它可能导致严重症状，影响一个人的感受、思维和处理日常活动的方式，例如睡眠、进食或工作。抑郁可影响任何人，不论年龄、性别、种族或族裔、收入、文化或教育程度。研究表明，遗传、生物、环境和心理因素在该障碍中起作用。女性被诊断为抑郁的频率高于男性，但男性也可能患抑郁。由于男性可能较不可能识别、谈论和为其负面感受寻求帮助，他们的抑郁症状未被诊断和治疗不足的风险更大。此外，抑郁可与其他精神障碍或慢性疾病同时发生，例如糖尿病、癌症、心脏病和慢性疼痛。抑郁可使这些状况恶化，反之亦然。有时，为某种疾病服用的药物会引起副作用，也会促成抑郁症状。

英文原文：
Everyone feels sad or low sometimes, but these feelings usually pass. Depression (also called major depression, major depressive disorder, or clinical depression) is different. It can cause severe symptoms that affect how a person feels, thinks, and handles daily activities, such as sleeping, eating, or working.
Depression can affect anyone regardless of age, sex, race or ethnicity, income, culture, or education. Research suggests that genetic, biological, environmental, and psychological factors play a role in the disorder.
Women are diagnosed with depression more often than men, but men can also be depressed. Because men may be less likely to recognize, talk about, and seek help for their negative feelings, they are at greater risk of their depression symptoms being undiagnosed and undertreated.
In addition, depression can co-occur with other mental disorders or chronic illnesses, such as diabetes, cancer, heart disease, and chronic pain. Depression can make these conditions worse and vice versa. Sometimes, medications taken for an illness cause side effects that contribute to depression symptoms as well.

metadata.title: 抑郁 / Depression
metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: What is depression? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
抑郁有两种常见类型。重性抑郁包括情绪低落或丧失兴趣的症状，大多数时间持续至少2周，并干扰日常活动。持续性抑郁障碍（也称为心境恶劣或恶劣心境障碍）由较轻的抑郁症状组成，但持续时间长得多，通常至少2年。其他类型的抑郁包括以下这些。季节性情感障碍随季节变化而出现和消失，症状通常始于深秋和初冬，并在春季和夏季消失。伴有精神病性症状的抑郁是一种严重的抑郁形式，患者会经历精神病性症状，如妄想或幻觉。双相障碍包括抑郁发作，以及躁狂发作（或较轻的轻躁狂发作），表现为异常高涨的情绪、更易激惹或活动水平增加。其他类型的抑郁可在女性一生的特定时间点发生。妊娠、产后时期、月经周期和绝经与身体和激素变化有关，这些变化可在某些人中引发抑郁发作。经前焦虑障碍是经前综合征（PMS）的一种更严重形式，发生在月经前几周。围产期抑郁发生在妊娠期间或分娩后。它不仅仅是许多新妈妈在分娩后经历的“产后情绪低落”。围绝经期抑郁影响一些处于绝经过渡期的女性。女性可能会经历强烈的易激惹、焦虑、悲伤或丧失愉悦感。

英文原文：
There are two common types of depression.
Major depression includes symptoms of depressed mood or loss of interest, most of the time for at least 2 weeks, that interfere with daily activities.
Persistent depressive disorder (also called dysthymia or dysthymic disorder) consists of less severe depression symptoms that last much longer, usually for at least 2 years.
Other types of depression include the following.
Seasonal affective disorder comes and goes with the seasons, with symptoms typically starting in the late fall and early winter and going away during the spring and summer.
Depression with symptoms of psychosis is a severe form of depression in which a person experiences psychosis symptoms, such as delusions or hallucinations.
Bipolar disorder involves depressive episodes, as well as manic episodes (or less severe hypomanic episodes) with unusually elevated mood, greater irritability, or increased activity level.
Additional types of depression can occur at specific points in a woman’s life. Pregnancy, the postpartum period, the menstrual cycle, and menopause are associated with physical and hormonal changes that can bring on a depressive episode in some people.
Premenstrual dysphoric disorder is a more severe form of premenstrual syndrome, or PMS, that occurs in the weeks before menstruation.
Perinatal depression occurs during pregnancy or after childbirth. It is more than the “baby blues” many new moms experience after giving birth.
Perimenopausal depression affects some women during the transition to menopause. Women may experience feelings of intense irritability, anxiety, sadness, or loss of enjoyment.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
抑郁的常见体征和症状包括：持续悲伤、焦虑或“空虚”的情绪；绝望或悲观的感觉；易怒、沮丧或烦躁不安的感觉；内疚、无价值感或无助感；对爱好和活动失去兴趣或乐趣；疲劳、缺乏精力或感觉行动迟缓；难以集中注意力、记忆或做决定；睡眠困难、清晨过早醒来或睡眠过多；食欲变化或非计划性的体重变化；没有明确躯体原因且治疗无效的身体疼痛、头痛、痉挛或消化问题；死亡或自杀的想法或自杀企图。抑郁还可能涉及其他情绪或行为变化，包括：愤怒或易怒增加；感到烦躁不安或紧张；变得退缩、消极或疏离；更多参与高风险活动；冲动性增加；酒精或药物使用增加；与家人和朋友隔离；无法履行职责或忽视其他重要角色；性欲和性表现问题。并非每个抑郁的人都会表现出所有这些症状。有些人只经历少数症状，而另一些人则经历许多症状。抑郁症状会干扰日常功能，并给经历这些症状的人带来显著痛苦。如果你表现出抑郁的体征或症状，且这些症状持续存在或没有消失，请与医疗保健提供者交谈。如果你在你认识的人身上看到抑郁的迹象，鼓励他们向心理健康专业人员寻求帮助。

英文原文：
Common signs and symptoms of depression include:
Persistent sad, anxious, or “empty” mood
Feelings of hopelessness or pessimism
Feelings of irritability, frustration‚ or restlessness
Feelings of guilt, worthlessness, or helplessness
Loss of interest or pleasure in hobbies and activities
Fatigue, lack of energy, or feeling slowed down
Difficulty concentrating, remembering, or making decisions
Difficulty sleeping, waking too early in the morning, or oversleeping
Changes in appetite or unplanned weight changes
Physical aches or pains, headaches, cramps, or digestive problems without a clear physical cause that do not go away with treatment
Thoughts of death or suicide or suicide attempts
Depression can also involve other changes in mood or behavior that include:
Increased anger or irritability
Feeling restless or on edge
Becoming withdrawn, negative, or detached
Increased engagement in high-risk activities
Greater impulsivity
Increased use of alcohol or drugs
Isolating from family and friends
Inability to meet responsibilities or ignoring other important roles
Problems with sexual desire and performance
Not everyone who is depressed shows all these symptoms. Some people experience only a few symptoms, while others experience many. Depression symptoms interfere with day-to-day functioning and cause significant distress for the person experiencing them.
If you show signs or symptoms of depression and they persist or do not go away, talk to a health care provider. If you see signs of depression in someone you know, encourage them to seek help from a mental health professional.

metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: What are the signs and symptoms of depression? / 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
要被诊断为抑郁，一个人必须在一天中的大部分时间、几乎每天都有症状，持续至少2周。其中一项症状必须是情绪低落，或对大多数活动失去兴趣或乐趣。儿童和青少年可能表现为易怒，而不是悲伤。尽管抑郁诊断需要除情绪低落外还存在若干持续症状，但只有少数症状的人也可能从治疗中获益。症状的严重程度和频率以及持续时间因人而异。如果你认为自己可能患有抑郁，请与医疗保健提供者交谈，例如初级保健医生、心理学家或精神科医生。就诊期间，提供者可能会询问你的症状何时开始、持续了多久、出现频率如何，以及是否妨碍你外出或进行日常活动。就诊前记录一些关于你症状的笔记可能会有帮助。某些药物和医学状况，例如病毒感染或甲状腺疾病，可引起与抑郁相同的症状。提供者可以通过进行体格检查、问诊和实验室检查来排除这些可能性。

英文原文：
To be diagnosed with depression, a person must have symptoms most of the day, nearly every day, for at least 2 weeks. One of the symptoms must be a depressed mood or a loss of interest or pleasure in most activities. Children and adolescents may be irritable rather than sad.
Although several persistent symptoms, in addition to low mood, are required for a depression diagnosis, people with only a few symptoms may benefit from treatment. The severity and frequency of symptoms and how long they last vary depending on the person.
If you think you may have depression, talk to a health care provider, such as a primary care doctor, psychologist, or psychiatrist. During the visit, the provider may ask when your symptoms began, how long they have lasted, how often they occur, and if they keep you from going out or doing your usual activities. It may help to take some notes about your symptoms before the visit.
Certain medications and medical conditions, such as viruses or thyroid disorders, can cause the same symptoms as depression. A provider can rule out these possibilities by doing a physical exam, interview, and lab tests.

metadata.section: How is depression diagnosed? / 专业评估 诊断

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
抑郁症对人的影响可能因年龄而异。儿童可能焦虑或暴躁、假装生病、拒绝上学、黏着父母，或担心父母可能去世。年龄较大的儿童和青少年可能在学校惹麻烦、闷闷不乐、容易受挫、感到坐立不安，或自尊心低下。他们可能患有其他障碍，如焦虑、进食障碍、注意缺陷/多动障碍或物质使用障碍。年龄较大的儿童和青少年也更可能经历过度嗜睡（称为嗜睡症）和食欲增加（称为贪食症）。年轻成人更可能易怒、抱怨体重增加和嗜睡，并对生活和未来持消极看法。他们常患有其他障碍，如广泛性焦虑障碍、社交恐惧症、惊恐障碍或物质使用障碍。中年成人可能有更多抑郁发作、性欲减退、半夜失眠或早醒。他们常报告胃部问题，如腹泻或便秘。老年人常感到悲伤、悲痛或其他不太明显的症状。他们可能报告缺乏情绪，而非抑郁心境。老年人也更可能患有其他可导致或促成抑郁的躯体疾病或疼痛。在严重病例中，记忆和思维问题（称为假性痴呆）可能很突出。抑郁症在男性和女性身上也可能表现不同，例如他们表现出的症状以及他们用来应对这些症状的行为。例如，男性（以及女性）可能表现出悲伤以外的症状，反而显得愤怒或易怒。对一些人来说，症状表现为躯体问题（例如，心跳加速、胸闷、慢性头痛或消化问题）。许多男性更可能就这些躯体症状而非情绪症状去看医疗保健提供者。虽然增加酒精或药物使用在任何人群中都可能是抑郁的迹象，但男性也更可能将这些物质用作应对策略。

英文原文：
Depression can affect people differently depending on their age.
Children may be anxious or cranky, pretend to be sick, refuse to go to school, cling to a parent, or worry that a parent may die.
Older children and teens may get into trouble at school, sulk, be easily frustrated‚ feel restless, or have low self-esteem. They may have other disorders, such as anxiety, an eating disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, or substance use disorder. Older children and teens are also more likely to experience excessive sleepiness (called hypersomnia) and increased appetite (called hyperphagia).
Young adults are more likely to be irritable, complain of weight gain and hypersomnia, and have a negative view of life and the future. They often have other disorders, such as generalized anxiety disorder, social phobia, panic disorder, or substance use disorder.
Middle-aged adults may have more depressive episodes, decreased libido, middle-of-the-night insomnia, or early morning waking. They often report stomach problems, such as diarrhea or constipation.
Older adults often feel sadness, grief, or other less obvious symptoms. They may report a lack of emotions rather than a depressed mood. Older adults are also more likely to have other medical conditions or pain that can cause or contribute to depression. Memory and thinking problems (called pseudodementia) may be prominent in severe cases.
Depression can also look different in men versus women, such as the symptoms they show and the behaviors they use to cope with them. For instance, men (as well as women) may show symptoms other than sadness, instead seeming angry or irritable.
For some people, symptoms manifest as physical problems (for example, a racing heart, tightened chest, chronic headaches, or digestive issues). Many men are more likely to see a health care provider about these physical symptoms than their emotional ones. While increased use of alcohol or drugs can be a sign of depression in any person, men are also more likely to use these substances as a coping strategy.

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
抑郁症的治疗通常包括心理治疗（面对面或虚拟）、药物治疗，或两者兼有。如果这些治疗不能充分减轻症状，脑刺激疗法可能是另一种选择。选择合适的治疗方案基于个人的需求、偏好和医疗状况，并与心理健康专业人士或医疗保健提供者协商。找到最佳治疗可能需要反复尝试。对于较轻的抑郁症，通常首先尝试心理治疗，如果单独心理治疗不能产生良好反应，则随后添加药物治疗。中度或重度抑郁症患者通常在初始治疗计划中就被开具药物。

英文原文：
Depression treatment typically involves psychotherapy (in person or virtual), medication, or both. If these treatments do not reduce symptoms sufficiently, brain stimulation therapy may be another option.
Choosing the right treatment plan is based on a person’s needs, preferences, and medical situation and in consultation with a mental health professional or a health care provider. Finding the best treatment may take trial and error.
For milder forms of depression, psychotherapy is often tried first, with medication added later if the therapy alone does not produce a good response. People with moderate or severe depression usually are prescribed medication as part of the initial treatment plan.

metadata.title: 抑郁 / Depression
metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: How is depression treated? / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
心理治疗（也称为谈话治疗或咨询）可以通过教授抑郁症患者新的思维和行为方式，并帮助他们改变导致抑郁的习惯来提供帮助。心理治疗由持证、受过培训的心理健康专业人员在一对一咨询或团体环境中进行。心理治疗当面进行或通过远程医疗虚拟进行均可有效。提供者可能使用数字或移动技术（如应用程序或其他工具）来支持或补充治疗。治疗抑郁症的循证疗法包括认知行为疗法和人际治疗。使用其他形式的心理治疗，如心理动力治疗，在有限时间内也可能帮助某些抑郁症患者。认知行为疗法（CBT）：通过CBT，人们学会挑战和改变无益的想法和行为，以改善他们的抑郁和焦虑情绪。CBT的最新进展包括加入正念原则，并将治疗专门针对特定症状，如失眠。人际治疗（IPT）：IPT专注于影响情绪的人际和生活事件，反之亦然。IPT旨在帮助人们改善关系中的沟通技巧，建立社会支持网络，并培养现实期望，以更好地应对可能导致或加重其抑郁的危机或其他问题。了解更多关于心理治疗的信息。

英文原文：
Psychotherapy (also called talk therapy or counseling) can help people with depression by teaching them new ways of thinking and behaving and helping them change habits that contribute to depression. Psychotherapy occurs under the care of a licensed, trained mental health professional in one-on-one sessions or with others in a group setting.
Psychotherapy can be effective when delivered in person or virtually via telehealth. A provider may support or supplement therapy using digital or mobile technology, like apps or other tools.
Evidence-based therapies to treat depression include cognitive behavioral therapy and interpersonal therapy. Using other forms of psychotherapy, such as psychodynamic therapy, for a limited time also may help some people with depression.
Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) : With CBT, people learn to challenge and change unhelpful thoughts and behaviors to improve their depressive and anxious feelings. Recent advances in CBT include adding mindfulness principles and specializing the therapy to target specific symptoms like insomnia.
Interpersonal therapy (IPT) : IPT focuses on interpersonal and life events that impact mood and vice versa. IPT aims to help people improve their communication skills within relationships, form social support networks, and develop realistic expectations to better deal with crises or other issues that may be contributing to or worsening their depression.
Learn more about psychotherapy .

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
FDA尚未批准任何用于治疗抑郁症的天然产品。尽管研究仍在进行且结果不一致，但一些人报告称，包括维生素D和草本膳食补充剂圣约翰草在内的天然产品有助于缓解其抑郁症状。然而，这些产品可能带来风险，包括在某些情况下与处方药发生相互作用。在未事先咨询医疗保健提供者的情况下，请勿使用维生素D、圣约翰草或其他膳食补充剂或天然产品。必须通过严谨的研究来检验这些及其他天然产品是否安全有效。

英文原文：
The FDA has not approved any natural products for treating depression. Although research is ongoing and findings are inconsistent, some people report that natural products, including vitamin D and the herbal dietary supplement St. John’s wort, helped their depression symptoms. However, these products can come with risks, including, in some cases, interactions with prescription medications.
Do not use vitamin D, St. John’s wort, or other dietary supplements or natural products without first talking to a health care provider. Rigorous studies must test whether these and other natural products are safe and effective.

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
大多数抑郁症患者能从心理健康治疗中获益。一旦开始治疗，你应当会逐渐感觉好转。在这段时间里，对自己宽容一些。试着做你过去喜欢做的事。即使你不想做，它们也能改善你的情绪。其他可能有帮助的事情：尝试进行身体活动。每天只需步行30分钟就能改善你的情绪。尽量保持规律的入睡和起床时间。规律、健康地饮食。能做多少做多少。确定哪些必须完成，哪些可以等待。与人联系。与你信任的人谈谈你的感受。推迟做出重大人生决定，直到你感觉好转。与熟悉你的人讨论决定。避免使用酒精、尼古丁或毒品，包括非为你处方的药物。

英文原文：
Most people with depression benefit from mental health treatment. Once you begin treatment, you should gradually start to feel better. Go easy on yourself during this time. Try to do things you used to enjoy. Even if you don’t feel like doing them, they can improve your mood.
Other things that may help:
Try to get physical activity. Just 30 minutes a day of walking can boost your mood.
Try to maintain a regular bedtime and wake-up time.
Eat regular, healthy meals.
Do what you can as you can. Decide what must get done and what can wait.
Connect with people. Talk to people you trust about how you are feeling.
Delay making important life decisions until you feel better. Discuss decisions with people who know you well.
Avoid using alcohol, nicotine, or drugs, including medications not prescribed for you.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
如果你认识的人患有抑郁症，帮助他们去看医疗保健提供者或心理健康专业人员。你还可以：提供支持、理解、耐心和鼓励。邀请他们出去散步、郊游和参加其他活动。帮助他们坚持治疗计划，例如设置提醒以服用处方药。确保他们有交通工具或能够参加治疗预约。提醒他们，随着时间和治疗，他们的抑郁症可以缓解。

英文原文：
If someone you know is depressed, help them see a health care provider or mental health professional. You also can:
Offer support, understanding, patience, and encouragement.
Invite them out for walks, outings, and other activities.
Help them stick to their treatment plan, such as setting reminders to take prescribed medications.
Make sure they have transportation or access to therapy appointments.
Remind them that, with time and treatment, their depression can lift.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
抑郁是一种常见但严重的心境障碍。研究表明，抑郁由遗传、生物、环境和心理因素共同导致。所有人都可能感到抑郁，但由于女性独特的生物、激素和社会经历，这种障碍在女性中尤为常见。抑郁并非由女性做过或未做过任何事情引起，也不是她能够“振作起来”就能摆脱的。大多数女性需要治疗才能好转。

英文原文：
Depression is a common but serious mood disorder. Research suggests that depression is caused by a combination of genetic, biological, environmental, and psychological factors.
All people can feel depressed, but the disorder is especially common among women due to unique biological, hormonal, and social experiences.
Depression is not brought on by anything a woman has or has not done, and it is not something she can “snap out” of. Most women need treatment to feel better.

metadata.title: 抑郁 / Depression in Women: 4 Things to Know
metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: 1. Depression is a medical condition. /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
悲伤只是抑郁的一部分。其他常见症状包括：焦虑或易怒；感到绝望、无价值或无助；对爱好和活动失去兴趣或乐趣；疲劳、缺乏精力或感觉行动迟缓；难以集中注意力、记忆或做决定；睡眠或食欲发生变化；没有明确生理原因的身体疼痛或酸痛；有死亡或自杀的念头或自杀未遂。这些症状可能使人难以思考、工作、睡眠、学习、进食和享受生活。如果你一天中大部分时间、几乎每天都有这些症状，并持续至少2周，请与医疗保健提供者交谈。抑郁对每个人来说表现不尽相同；有些女性可能经历许多症状，而另一些女性可能只经历少数症状。与医疗保健提供者良好沟通可以改善你的照护。了解获得帮助的方法，并寻找医疗保健提供者或获得治疗。寻找与医疗保健提供者交谈的技巧，以改善你的照护并充分利用你的就诊。

英文原文：
Sadness is only one part of depression. Other common symptoms include:
Anxiety or irritability
Feelings of hopelessness, worthlessness, or helplessness
Loss of interest or pleasure in hobbies and activities
Fatigue, lack of energy, or feeling slowed down
Difficulty concentrating, remembering, or making decisions
Changes in sleep or appetite
Physical aches or pains that do not have a clear physical cause
Thoughts of death or suicide or suicide attempts
These symptoms can make it hard to think, work, sleep, study, eat, and enjoy life. Talk to a health care provider if you experience symptoms most of the day, nearly every day, for at least 2 weeks. Depression does not look the same for everyone; some women may experience many symptoms, and others may experience only a few.
Communicating well with a health care provider can improve your care. Learn about ways to get help and find a health care provider or access treatment. Find tips for talking with a health care provider to improve your care and get the most out of your visit.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
某些类型的抑郁发生在女性生命中的特定阶段。怀孕、产后时期、月经周期和围绝经期伴随着身体和激素变化，这些变化可能在某些女性中引发抑郁发作。经前焦虑障碍是经前综合征（PMS）的一种更严重形式，发生在月经前几周。该障碍会导致严重症状，如情绪低落、愤怒或易怒、自杀念头、食欲变化、腹胀、乳房胀痛以及关节或肌肉疼痛。围产期抑郁发生在怀孕期间或分娩后。它不仅仅是许多新妈妈在分娩后经历的“产后情绪低落”。患有围产期抑郁的女性会感到极度悲伤、焦虑和疲劳，这可能使她们难以完成日常任务，包括照顾自己或他人。了解更多关于围产期抑郁的信息。围绝经期抑郁影响一些处于向绝经过渡期间的女性。虽然月经异常、睡眠问题、情绪波动和潮热在绝经过渡期很常见，但更极端的易怒、焦虑、悲伤或丧失愉悦感可能是抑郁的迹象。

英文原文：
Certain types of depression occur at specific stages of a woman’s life. Pregnancy, the postpartum period, the menstrual cycle, and perimenopause are associated with physical and hormonal changes that can bring on a depressive episode in some women.
Premenstrual dysphoric disorder is a more intense form of premenstrual syndrome, or PMS, that occurs in the weeks before menstruation. The disorder causes severe symptoms, such as depressed mood, anger or irritability, suicidal thoughts, appetite changes, bloating, breast tenderness, and joint or muscle pain.
Perinatal depression occurs during pregnancy or after childbirth. It is more than the “baby blues” many new moms experience after giving birth. Women with perinatal depression feel extreme sadness, anxiety, and fatigue that may make it difficult to carry out daily tasks, including caring for themselves or others. Learn more about perinatal depression .
Perimenopausal depression affects some women during the transition to menopause. Whereas abnormal periods, problems sleeping, mood swings, and hot flashes are common during the menopause transition, more extreme feelings of irritability, anxiety, sadness, or loss of enjoyment may be signs of depression.

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
即使是最严重的抑郁也可以治疗。常见的治疗方法有抗抑郁药物、谈话治疗（线上或线下），或药物与治疗相结合。治疗没有“一刀切”的方案。可能需要反复尝试才能找到最适合你的方法。医疗保健提供者可以解释不同的选择，并帮助你根据症状选择最佳治疗。在帮助下，你可以感觉更好。了解更多关于抑郁治疗的信息。

英文原文：
Even the most severe depression can be treated. Common treatments are antidepressant medication, talk therapy (virtual or in person), or a combination of medication and therapy.
There is no “one-size-fits-all” for treatment. It may take trial and error to find the best one for you. A health care provider can explain the different options and help you choose the best treatment based on your symptoms. With help, you can feel better.
Learn more about treatments for depression .

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
围产期抑郁包括在怀孕期间发生的抑郁（产前抑郁）以及分娩后数周和数月内发生的抑郁（产后抑郁）。大多数围产期抑郁发作始于婴儿出生后4至8周内。患有围产期抑郁的孕妇和产后女性会经历极度悲伤、焦虑和疲劳，这可能使其难以完成日常任务，包括照顾自己或他人。

英文原文：
Perinatal depression includes depression that occurs during pregnancy (prenatal depression) and in the weeks and months after childbirth (postpartum depression). Most episodes of perinatal depression begin within 4−8 weeks after the baby is born. Pregnant and postpartum women with perinatal depression experience extreme sadness, anxiety, and fatigue that may make it difficult to carry out daily tasks, including caring for themselves or others.

metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: What is perinatal depression? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
“产后情绪低落”是一个术语，用于描述许多女性在分娩后前2周内经历的轻微且短暂的情绪变化以及担忧、不快乐和疲惫感。婴儿需要全天候的照顾，因此新妈妈有时感到疲倦或不堪重负是正常的。分娩后情绪变化以及焦虑或不快乐的感觉严重或持续超过2周，可能是产后抑郁的迹象。患有产后抑郁的女性如果不接受治疗，通常不会感觉好转。

英文原文：
“Baby blues” is a term used to describe mild and short-lasting mood changes and feelings of worry, unhappiness, and exhaustion that many women experience in the first 2 weeks after giving birth. Babies require around-the-clock care, so it’s normal for new mothers to feel tired or overwhelmed sometimes.
Mood changes and feelings of anxiety or unhappiness that are severe or last longer than 2 weeks after childbirth may be signs of postpartum depression. Women with postpartum depression generally will not feel better without treatment.

metadata.title: 抑郁 / Perinatal Depression
metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: How is postpartum depression different from “baby blues”? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
有些女性会经历围产期抑郁的少数症状，而另一些女性则会经历多种症状。一些较常见的症状包括：一天中大部分时间、几乎每天，持续至少2周的情绪悲伤、焦虑或“空虚”感到绝望或悲观感到易怒、沮丧或烦躁感到内疚、无价值或无助对爱好和活动失去兴趣或乐趣疲劳或精力异常下降坐立不安或难以静坐难以集中注意力、记忆或做决定睡眠困难（即使婴儿睡着时）、清晨早醒或睡眠过多食欲异常变化或非计划性体重变化没有明确生理原因且治疗无法缓解的身体疼痛、头痛、痉挛或消化问题难以与婴儿建立联结或形成情感依恋持续怀疑自己照顾婴儿的能力死亡念头或伤害自己或婴儿的念头或自杀企图经历任何这些症状的女性应去看医疗保健提供者。提供者可以判断这些症状是由围产期抑郁还是其他原因所致。

英文原文：
Some women experience a few symptoms of perinatal depression, while others experience several symptoms. Some of the more common symptoms include:
Persistent sad, anxious, or “empty” mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least 2 weeks
Feelings of hopelessness or pessimism
Feelings of irritability, frustration, or restlessness
Feelings of guilt, worthlessness, or helplessness
Loss of interest or pleasure in hobbies and activities
Fatigue or abnormal decrease in energy
Being restless or having trouble sitting still
Difficulty concentrating, remembering, or making decisions
Difficulty sleeping (even when the baby is asleep), waking early in the morning, or oversleeping
Abnormal changes in appetite or unplanned weight changes
Physical aches or pains, headaches, cramps, or digestive problems that do not have a clear physical cause and do not go away with treatment
Trouble bonding or forming an emotional attachment with the baby
Persistent doubts about the ability to care for the baby
Thoughts of death or harming oneself or the baby or suicide attempts
Women who experience any of these symptoms should see a health care provider. A provider can determine whether the symptoms are due to perinatal depression or something else.

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
产后精神病是一种可能在分娩后发生的严重精神疾病。患有产后精神病的女性可能会经历妄想（不真实的想法或信念）、幻觉（看到、听到或闻到不存在的事物）、躁狂（一种高涨、兴奋的情绪，通常似乎与现实脱节）、偏执和混乱。

英文原文：
Postpartum psychosis is a serious mental illness that can occur after childbirth. Women with postpartum psychosis may experience delusions (thoughts or beliefs that are not true), hallucinations (seeing, hearing, or smelling things that are not there), mania (a high, elated mood that often seems out of touch with reality), paranoia, and confusion.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
围产期抑郁是一种医学状况，可能影响任何孕妇或产后女性，无论其年龄、种族、族裔、收入、文化或教育程度如何。女性不应因患有围产期抑郁而受到责备或被认为有过错：这不是由她做过或未做过的任何事情引起的。围产期抑郁没有单一原因。研究表明，遗传和环境因素对该障碍有影响。导致围产期抑郁的具体因素可能包括：生活压力（例如，工作要求或过往创伤经历）分娩和照顾新生儿的身体和情感需求怀孕期间和之后发生的激素变化此外，如果女性有抑郁或双相障碍的个人史或家族史，或者如果她在之前怀孕时经历过抑郁，那么她患围产期抑郁的风险会增加。有围产期抑郁史的女性应咨询医疗保健提供者，制定后续护理计划，以防抑郁发作再次发生。

英文原文：
Perinatal depression is a medical condition that can affect any pregnant or postpartum woman, regardless of age, race, ethnicity, income, culture, or education. A woman is not to blame or at fault for having perinatal depression: It is not caused by anything she has or has not done.
Perinatal depression does not have a single cause. Research suggests that genetic and environmental factors contribute to the disorder. Specific factors contributing to perinatal depression can include:
Life stress (for example, demands at work or experiences of past trauma)
Physical and emotional demands of childbirth and caring for a new baby
Changes in hormones that occur during and after pregnancy
In addition, women are at increased risk for perinatal depression if they have a personal or family history of depression or bipolar disorder or if they experienced depression with a previous pregnancy. Women with a history of perinatal depression should consult a health care provider to develop a plan for follow-up care in case a depressive episode reoccurs.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
治疗围产期抑郁对母亲及其婴儿的健康至关重要，因为该障碍可对二者产生严重影响。然而，经过适当治疗，大多数女性会感觉好转，其症状也会改善。围产期抑郁的治疗通常包括心理治疗、药物治疗，或心理治疗与药物治疗相结合。研究人员仍在继续研究围产期抑郁的治疗方案。医疗保健提供者可解释不同的治疗方法，并帮助您根据自身症状选择最佳方案。了解更多关于治疗抑郁的方法。了解获取帮助、寻找医疗保健提供者或获得治疗的途径。

英文原文：
Treating perinatal depression is critical for the health of the mother and her baby, as the disorder can have serious effects on both. However, with proper treatment, most women feel better and their symptoms improve.
Treatment for perinatal depression usually includes therapy, medication, or a combination of therapy and medication.
Researchers continue to study treatment options for perinatal depression. A health care provider can explain the different treatments and help you choose the best one based on your symptoms. Learn more about approaches for treating depression .
Learn about ways to get help and find a health care provider or access treatment.

metadata.title: 抑郁 / Perinatal Depression
metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: How is perinatal depression treated? / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
几种心理治疗（也称为谈话治疗或咨询）可以通过教授新的思维和行为方式，帮助围产期抑郁女性改变导致抑郁的习惯。针对围产期抑郁的循证治疗包括认知行为治疗和人际治疗。认知行为治疗（CBT）：通过CBT，人们学习挑战和改变无益的想法和行为，以改善抑郁和焦虑情绪。人们还学习对情境的不同反应方式。CBT可以单独进行，也可以与有类似困扰的一组人一起进行。人际治疗（IPT）：IPT基于人际和生活事件影响情绪、反之亦然的理念。IPT旨在帮助人们改善人际关系中的沟通技巧，建立社会支持网络，并形成现实的期望，以更好地应对危机或其他导致抑郁的问题。了解更多关于心理治疗的信息。

英文原文：
Several types of psychotherapy (also called talk therapy or counseling) can help women with perinatal depression by teaching them new ways of thinking and behaving and helping them change habits that contribute to depression. Evidence-based therapies for perinatal depression include cognitive behavioral therapy and interpersonal therapy.
Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) : With CBT, people learn to challenge and change unhelpful thoughts and behaviors to improve their depressive and anxious feelings. People also learn different ways of reacting to situations. CBT can be conducted individually or with a group of people who have similar concerns.
Interpersonal therapy (IPT) : IPT is based on the idea that interpersonal and life events impact mood and vice versa. IPT aims to help people improve their communication skills within relationships, form social support networks, and develop realistic expectations to better deal with crises or other issues contributing to their depression.
Learn more about psychotherapy .

metadata.title: 抑郁 / Perinatal Depression
metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: Psychotherapy / 治疗 心理治疗 应对方法

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
如果你认为自己患有围产期抑郁，首先预约一位医疗保健提供者。这可以是初级保健医生，也可以是专门诊断和治疗精神障碍的心理健康专业人员（例如，心理学家、精神科医生或社会工作者）。医疗保健提供者将对你进行检查，并与你讨论治疗方案和后续步骤，包括如果你怀孕或哺乳时的选择。与医疗保健提供者良好沟通可以改善你的护理，并帮助你们双方就你的健康做出良好选择。查找与医疗保健提供者交谈的技巧，以改善你的护理并充分利用你的就诊。如需更多资源，包括要向提供者提出的问题，请访问医疗保健研究与质量局网站。药物滥用和心理健康服务管理局有一个在线治疗定位器，可帮助你在所在地区找到心理健康服务。

英文原文：
If you think you have perinatal depression, start by making an appointment with a health care provider. This could be a primary care doctor or a mental health professional who specializes in diagnosing and treating mental disorders (for example, a psychologist, psychiatrist, or social worker). A health care provider will examine you and talk to you about treatment options and next steps, including options if you are pregnant or nursing.
Communicating well with a health care provider can improve your care and help you both make good choices about your health. Find tips for talking with a health care provider to improve your care and get the most out of your visit. For additional resources, including questions to ask a provider, visit the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality website .
The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration has an online treatment locator to help you find mental health services in your area.

必须理解，围产期抑郁是一种影响母亲、孩子和家庭的医学状况。治疗是康复的核心。配偶、伴侣、家庭成员和朋友可能是最先识别出新妈妈抑郁迹象的人。家人和朋友可以通过多种方式提供帮助，包括：鼓励与医疗保健提供者讨论、帮助赴约、提供情感或实际支持、协助日常事务，如照顾婴儿或家庭。

英文原文：
It is essential to understand that perinatal depression is a medical condition that impacts the mother, the child, and the family. Treatment is central to recovery.
Spouses, partners, family members, and friends may be the first to recognize signs of depression in a new mother. Family and friends can provide help in many ways that include:
Encouraging discussion with a health care provider
Helping get to appointments
Offering emotional or practical support
Assisting with daily tasks such as caring for the baby or home

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
抑郁 / 青少年抑郁：不仅仅是情绪波动

我有抑郁吗？

你是否经常感到悲伤、焦虑、毫无价值，甚至“空虚”？你是否对曾经喜欢的活动失去兴趣？你是否容易沮丧、烦躁或生气？你是否发现自己疏远朋友和家人？你的成绩是否在下降？你的饮食或睡眠习惯是否发生了变化？你是否经历过任何疲劳或记忆丧失？你是否想过自杀或伤害自己？抑郁对每个人来说表现不同。你可能有许多上述症状，也可能只有少数几个。

英文原文：
Do you often feel sad, anxious, worthless, or even “empty”?
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?
Do you get easily frustrated, irritable, or angry?
Do you find yourself withdrawing from friends and family?
Are your grades dropping?
Have your eating or sleeping habits changed?
Have you experienced any fatigue or memory loss?
Have you thought about suicide or harming yourself?
Depression looks different for everyone. You might have many of the symptoms listed above or just a few.

metadata.title: 抑郁 / Teen Depression: More Than Just Moodiness
metadata.keywords: 抑郁 情绪低落 失去兴趣 心情
metadata.section: Do I have depression? /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
与你信任的成年人（如你的父母或监护人、老师或学校咨询师）谈谈你的感受。向你的医生咨询专业帮助的选项。抑郁症可以通过心理治疗（也称为“谈话治疗”）、药物或药物与谈话治疗相结合来治疗。尽量花时间与朋友或家人在一起，即使你不想这样做。保持活跃和锻炼，即使只是去散步。体育活动会释放你大脑中的化学物质，如内啡肽，可以帮助你感觉更好。尽量保持规律的睡眠时间表。吃健康的食物。美国卫生与公众服务部 美国国立卫生研究院 NIMH 识别号 OM 22-4321

英文原文：
Talk to a trusted adult (such as your parent or guardian, teacher, or school counselor) about how you’ve been feeling.
Ask your doctor about options for professional help. Depression can be treated with psychotherapy (also called “talk therapy”), medication, or a combination of medication and talk therapy.
Try to spend time with friends or family, even if you don’t feel like you want to.
Stay active and exercise, even if it’s just going for a walk. Physical activity releases chemicals, such as endorphins, in your brain that can help you feel better.
Try to keep a regular sleep schedule.
Eat healthy foods.
U.S. DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES National Institutes of Health NIMH Identification No. OM 22-4321

中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
注意缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）的特征是持续存在的注意力不集中和/或过度活跃及冲动模式，使人在至少两个生活领域（如家庭、学校或工作）中难以正常运作。患有ADHD的成年人可能会经历以下类型的症状：注意力不集中：难以集中注意力、保持任务专注或保持条理；过度活跃：过度活动或坐立不安，即使在不适当的场合也是如此，并且难以参与安静的活动；冲动：不假思索地行动或难以自我控制。根据其症状，一个人可被诊断为三种类型的ADHD之一：注意力不集中型、过度活跃-冲动型或混合型。患有ADHD的成年人通常有学业成绩不佳、工作问题或关系紧张的病史。他们可能会发现保持条理、坚持一份工作、遵守预约、执行日常任务或完成大型项目具有挑战性。他们可能坐立不安，试图同时做多件事，或参与冒险或冲动的行为。ADHD被认为是一种发育障碍，因为症状必须始于童年——但许多成年人也患有ADHD。

英文原文：
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is marked by a persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity and impulsivity that makes it hard to function in at least two areas of life, such as at home, school, or work.
Adults with ADHD may experience the following types of symptoms:
Inattention : Difficulty paying attention, staying on task, or being organized
Hyperactivity : Excessive activity or restlessness, even at inappropriate times, and difficulty engaging in quiet activities
Impulsivity : Acting without thinking or having trouble with self-control
Based on their symptoms, a person can be diagnosed with one of three types of ADHD: inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive, or combined.
Adults with ADHD often have a history of poor academic performance, work problems, or strained relationships. They may find it challenging to stay organized, stick to a job, keep appointments, perform daily tasks, or complete large projects. They may be restless, try to do multiple things at once, or engage in risky or impulsive behaviors.
ADHD is considered a developmental disorder because symptoms must begin in childhood—but many adults also have ADHD.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
注意缺陷多动障碍 / 成人ADHD：需要了解的4件事

2. ADHD症状可能给日常生活带来问题。

ADHD症状会干扰日常功能。在成人中，症状可能导致：

难以集中注意力，且经常分心
缺乏条理和拖延
时间管理、计划或组织能力差
记不住日常任务
经常丢东西或在活动中健忘
经常打断他人或非常健谈
难以专注于一项大任务或多任务处理
难以遵循指示或完成项目
难以长时间坐着不动，经常移动或坐立不安
感到不安，需要持续活动或刺激
选择即时奖励而非未来奖励或后果

许多人在某些时候会表现出其中一些行为。然而，对于患有ADHD的成人，这些行为更严重、更频繁、更持久，干扰日常生活，在多种情境中出现，并持续至少6个月。

ADHD常与其他精神障碍共病，并可能使其更难治疗。睡眠问题尤为普遍，影响高达70%的ADHD成人。

对于许多ADHD患者，症状会持续到成年期，但可能随年龄而变化。例如，注意缺陷症状往往随年龄增长而持续，而多动和冲动则更可能减轻。了解更多关于ADHD的症状和类型。

英文原文：
ADHD symptoms interfere with daily functioning. In adults, symptoms can lead to:
Difficulty paying attention and often getting distracted
Disorganization and procrastination
Poor time management, planning, or organization
Trouble remembering daily tasks
Frequently losing things or being forgetful in activities
Frequently interrupting others or being very talkative
Trouble focusing on a large task or multitasking
Trouble following instructions or finishing projects
Difficulty sitting still for long periods and often moving or fidgeting
Feelings of restlessness and a need for constant activity or stimulation
Choosing immediate rewards over future rewards or consequences
Many people show some of these behaviors some of the time. However, for adults with ADHD, they are more severe, frequent, and persistent, interfering with daily life, occurring across multiple situations, and lasting at least 6 months.
ADHD often co-occurs with other mental disorders and can make them harder to treat. Sleep problems are especially prevalent, affecting up to 70% of adults with ADHD.
Symptoms continue into adulthood for many people with ADHD, but they may change with age. For instance, inattentive symptoms often persist as people get older, whereas hyperactivity and impulsivity are more likely to decline. Learn more about symptoms and types of ADHD .

注意缺陷多动障碍可在儿童期或成年期被诊断。然而，成人必须更早出现症状，始于12岁之前。诊断儿童与成人注意缺陷多动障碍的主要区别在于症状数量。成人或16岁以上的青少年必须表现出五条（而非六条）注意力不集中或活动过度和冲动的症状。

英文原文：
ADHD can be diagnosed in childhood or adulthood. However, adults must have shown symptoms much earlier, starting before age 12.
The main difference between diagnosing ADHD in children and adults is the number of symptoms. Adults or adolescents over 16 years must show five (instead of six) symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity and impulsivity.

metadata.section: 3. ADHD is diagnosed differently in children and adults. / 专业评估 诊断

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
在成年期诊断注意缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）较为复杂，因为需要证明症状在12岁之前就已出现。因此，诊断在很大程度上依赖于过去的行为报告。为了帮助诊断ADHD，初级保健提供者或心理健康专业人员可能会要求与熟悉您的人交谈，例如伴侣、家庭成员和朋友，以了解您在不同情境下以及童年时期的行为。他们可能会查看学校报告或其他童年记录。提供者还会与您交谈，并可能要求您完成以下事项：完成临床访谈、行为评定量表或症状检查表，以确定您是否符合ADHD的诊断标准。进行心理测试，评估认知过程，如记忆、计划、决策、推理和思维，以识别优势和挑战以及可能的学习障碍。报告您的情绪以及当前和过去的医疗状况，以排除其他诊断并制定整体治疗计划。

英文原文：
Diagnosing ADHD in adulthood is complicated by the need to show symptoms before age 12. For this reason, a diagnosis relies heavily on past reports of behavior.
To help diagnose ADHD, a primary care provider or mental health professional may ask to talk to people who know you well, such as a partner, family members, and friends, to learn about your behavior in different situations and during childhood. They may look at school reports or other childhood records.
A provider will also talk to you and may ask you to do the following:
Complete clinical interviews, behavior rating scales, or symptom checklists to determine whether you meet the criteria for a diagnosis of ADHD.
Take psychological tests that look at cognitive processes, such as memory, planning, decision-making, reasoning, and thinking, to identify strengths and challenges and possible learning disabilities.
Report on your mood and current and past medical conditions to rule out alternative diagnoses and establish an overall treatment plan.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
注意缺陷多动障碍 / 成人ADHD：需要了解的4件事

为什么我早先没有被诊断出ADHD？ / 专业评估 诊断

一个人可能直到成年才被诊断出ADHD，原因有很多。例如，你的老师和父母可能没有识别出这种障碍，或者可能提供了支持性环境，帮助你在有这种障碍的情况下仍能茁壮成长。或者你可能患有较轻形式的ADHD，在面临成年期的压力和要求之前，尤其是工作方面，一直可以得到良好管理。女孩和女性的ADHD症状在童年时期尤其容易被遗漏。诊断率上的性别差异在成年期开始趋于平衡。寻求ADHD以及可能同时出现的任何其他心理健康状况的诊断和治疗，永远不会太晚。有效的治疗可以让许多成年人及其家人的日常生活更轻松。查找与医疗保健提供者交谈的提示。你可以在NIMH网站上了解更多关于寻求帮助的信息。你也可以在药物滥用和心理健康服务管理局（SAMHSA）网站上了解如何在你的地区寻找支持和定位心理健康服务。

英文原文：
There are many reasons someone may not be diagnosed with ADHD until adulthood. For instance, your teachers and parents may not have recognized the disorder or may have provided supportive environments that helped you thrive despite it. Or you may have a milder form of ADHD that could be managed well until faced with the stresses and demands of adulthood, especially at work.
ADHD symptoms among girls and women are especially likely to have been missed in childhood. Sex differences in diagnosis rates begin to even out in adulthood.
It is never too late to seek a diagnosis and treatment for ADHD and any other mental health condition that may occur with it. Effective treatment can make day-to-day life easier for many adults and their families. Find tips for talking with a health care provider .
You can learn more about getting help on the NIMH website. You can also learn about finding support and locating mental health services in your area on the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) website.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
注意缺陷多动障碍的治疗可以减轻症状并改善功能。成人注意缺陷多动障碍最常见的治疗方法是：药物治疗，通常是兴奋剂类药物心理治疗，如行为治疗和认知行为治疗有效的治疗通常涉及多种要素的组合。有时，人们必须尝试几种治疗才能找到适合自己的方法。了解更多关于兴奋剂和其他心理健康药物。了解更多关于心理治疗。一些成人可能会发现，从生活教练或注意缺陷多动障碍教练那里获得支持很有帮助，他们可以教授执行功能技能以改善日常功能。其他人则尝试改变生活方式，例如在日常安排中增加更多体育锻炼。注意缺陷多动障碍症状导致工作受损的人可能有资格根据《美国残疾人法案》（ADA）获得合理便利。

英文原文：
Treatment for ADHD can reduce symptoms and improve functioning. The most common treatments for ADHD in adults are:
Medication, usually stimulant medications
Psychotherapy, like behavioral and cognitive behavioral therapy
Effective treatment often involves a combination of elements. Sometimes, people must try several treatments before finding the one that works for them.
Learn more about stimulants and other mental health medications . Learn more about psychotherapy .
Some adults may find it helpful to get support from a life coach or ADHD coach who can teach them executive function skills to improve daily functioning. Others try lifestyle changes, like adding more physical exercise to their daily schedule.
People whose ADHD symptoms cause impairment at work may qualify for reasonable accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) .

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
双相障碍是一种精神疾病，可以是慢性的（持续存在或不断复发）或发作性的（偶尔发生且间隔不规律）。人们有时用较早的术语躁狂抑郁性障碍或躁狂抑郁症来指代双相障碍。每个人都会经历情绪起伏，但在双相障碍中，情绪变化的范围可能极为极端。患有该障碍的人会出现躁狂发作或异常高涨的情绪，此时此人可能感到过度愉快、易怒或“亢奋”，与平时的自己相比活动水平显著增加。他们也可能出现抑郁发作，此时他们感到悲伤、冷漠或绝望，同时活动水平极低且无法正常运作。有些人会出现轻躁狂发作，其类似于躁狂发作但严重程度较轻，对日常生活的干扰也较小。大多数情况下，双相障碍的症状始于青春期晚期或成年早期。偶尔，儿童也可能出现双相障碍症状。尽管症状可能时有时无，但双相障碍通常需要终身治疗，不会自行消失。双相障碍可能是自杀、失业、功能能力和家庭不和的重要因素。然而，适当的治疗可以带来更好的功能和改善的生活质量。

英文原文：
Bipolar disorder is a mental illness that can be chronic (persistent or constantly recurring) or episodic (occurring occasionally and at irregular intervals). People sometimes refer to bipolar disorder with the older terms manic-depressive disorder or manic depression.
Everyone experiences ups and downs, but with bipolar disorder, the range of mood changes can be extreme. People with the disorder have manic episodes or unusually elevated moods in which the person might feel excessively happy, irritable, or “up,” with a marked increase in activity level compared to their usual self. They might also have depressive episodes, in which they feel sad, indifferent, or hopeless, combined with a very low activity level and an inability to function. Some people have hypomanic episodes, which are like manic episodes but are less severe, and don’t interfere as much with daily life.
Most of the time, bipolar disorder symptoms start during late adolescence or early adulthood. Occasionally, children may experience bipolar disorder symptoms.
Although symptoms may come and go, bipolar disorder usually requires lifelong treatment and does not go away on its own. Bipolar disorder can be an important factor in suicide, job loss, ability to function, and family discord. However, proper treatment can lead to better functioning and improved quality of life.

metadata.title: 双相障碍 / Bipolar Disorder
metadata.keywords: 双相障碍 躁狂 心境 情绪波动
metadata.section: What is bipolar disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
双相障碍的症状可能各不相同。患有该障碍的个体可能经历躁狂发作、抑郁发作或“混合”发作。混合发作同时具有躁狂和抑郁症状。这些心境发作所引起的症状持续一两周，有时更长。在一次发作期间，症状每天持续，且在一天中的大部分时间都存在。感受强烈，并伴随他人可察觉的行为、精力水平或活动水平的改变。在发作间歇期，心境通常恢复到健康基线。但在许多情况下，若没有充分治疗，随着时间推移，发作会变得更加频繁。有些双相障碍患者的症状可能比其他人更轻。例如，轻躁狂发作可能使个体感觉非常好且富有成效；他们可能不觉得有任何问题。然而，家人和朋友可能会注意到情绪波动和活动水平的改变属于异常行为，而抑郁发作可能紧随轻躁狂发作之后。

英文原文：
Symptoms of bipolar disorder can vary. An individual with the disorder may have manic episodes, depressive episodes, or “mixed” episodes. A mixed episode has both manic and depressive symptoms.
These mood episodes cause symptoms that last a week or two, or sometimes longer. During an episode, the symptoms last every day for most of the day. Feelings are intense and happen with changes in behavior, energy levels, or activity levels that are noticeable to others. In between episodes, mood usually returns to a healthy baseline. But in many cases, without adequate treatment, episodes occur more frequently as time goes on.
Some people with bipolar disorder may have milder symptoms than others. For example, hypomanic episodes may make an individual feel very good and productive; they may not feel like anything is wrong. However, family and friends may notice mood swings and changes in activity levels as unusual behavior, and depressive episodes may follow hypomanic episodes.

metadata.title: 双相障碍 / Bipolar Disorder

metadata.section: What are the symptoms of bipolar disorder? / 定义 含义 什么是 常见表现 症状 识别

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
人们被诊断出三种基本类型的双相障碍，这些类型涉及情绪、精力和活动水平的明显变化。这些情绪从躁狂发作到抑郁发作不等。双相Ⅰ型障碍的定义是躁狂发作持续至少7天（一天中大部分时间，几乎每天），或者躁狂症状严重到需要住院治疗。通常，也会出现单独的抑郁发作，通常持续至少2周。也可能出现具有混合特征的的情绪紊乱发作。一年内经历四次或更多次躁狂或抑郁发作被称为“快速循环”。双相Ⅱ型障碍的定义是抑郁和轻躁狂发作的模式，但轻躁狂发作的严重程度低于双相Ⅰ型障碍中的躁狂发作。许多双相Ⅱ型障碍患者长期处于持续性、低度抑郁状态。环性情感障碍（也称为环性心境）的定义是反复出现的轻躁狂和抑郁症状，其强度不足以或持续时间不够长，不足以被认定为轻躁狂或抑郁发作。“其他特定和未特定的双相及相关障碍”是一个诊断，指的是不符合上述三种主要双相障碍类型的双相障碍症状。

英文原文：
People are diagnosed with three basic types of bipolar disorder that involve clear changes in mood, energy, and activity levels. These moods range from manic episodes to depressive episodes.
Bipolar I disorder is defined by manic episodes that last at least 7 days (most of the day, nearly every day) or when manic symptoms are so severe that hospital care is needed. Usually, separate depressive episodes occur as well, typically lasting at least 2 weeks. Episodes of mood disturbance with mixed features are also possible. The experience of four or more episodes of mania or depression within a year is termed “rapid cycling.”
Bipolar II disorder is defined by a pattern of depressive and hypomanic episodes, but the hypomanic episodes are less severe than the manic episodes in bipolar I disorder. Many people with bipolar II disorder spend extended periods in a persistent, low-grade depressive state.
Cyclothymic disorder (also called cyclothymia) is defined by recurrent hypomanic and depressive symptoms that are not intense enough or do not last long enough to qualify as hypomanic or depressive episodes.
“Other specified and unspecified bipolar and related disorders” is a diagnosis that refers to bipolar disorder symptoms that do not match the three major types of bipolar disorder outlined above.

英文原文：
The exact cause of bipolar disorder is unknown. However, research suggests that a combination of factors may contribute to the illness.

metadata.title: 双相障碍 / Bipolar Disorder
metadata.keywords: 双相障碍 躁狂 心境 情绪波动
metadata.section: What causes bipolar disorder? / 影响因素 风险因素

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
双相障碍常呈家族聚集，研究表明这主要由遗传解释——携带某些基因的人比其他人更易患双相障碍。涉及许多基因，没有任何一个基因能导致该障碍。但基因并非唯一因素。对同卵双胞胎的研究显示，一个双胞胎可能患双相障碍，而另一个不会。尽管父母或兄弟姐妹患有双相障碍的人更可能患病，但并非所有有双相障碍家族史的人都会患病。研究还表明，具有双相障碍遗传风险的人在经历创伤或其他应激性生活事件后可能更易患病。

英文原文：
Bipolar disorder often runs in families, and research suggests this is mostly explained by heredity—people with certain genes are more likely to develop bipolar disorder than others. Many genes are involved, and no one gene can cause the disorder.
But genes are not the only factor. Studies of identical twins have shown that one twin can develop bipolar disorder while the other does not. Though people with a parent or sibling with bipolar disorder are more likely to develop it, not everyone with a family history of bipolar disorder will develop it. Research also suggests that people with a genetic risk of having bipolar disorder may be more likely to develop it after experiencing trauma or other stressful life events.

metadata.title: 双相障碍 / Bipolar Disorder

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
研究表明，双相障碍患者的大脑结构和功能可能与没有双相障碍或其他精神障碍的人不同。了解这些大脑变化的本质有助于研究人员更好地理解双相障碍，并且将来可能有助于预测哪种类型的治疗对双相障碍患者最有效。

英文原文：
Research shows that the brain structure and function of people with bipolar disorder may differ from those of people who do not have bipolar disorder or other mental disorders. Learning about the nature of these brain changes helps researchers better understand bipolar disorder and, in the future, may help predict which types of treatment will work best for a person with bipolar disorder.

metadata.section: Brain structure and function /

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
要诊断双相障碍，医疗保健提供者可能会完成体格检查，安排医学检测以排除其他疾病，并将该人转介给心理健康专业人员进行评估。双相障碍的诊断基于个体一生中症状和经历的严重程度、持续时间及频率，以及其家族史。有些人患双相障碍多年后才被诊断出来，原因有几个。双相II型障碍患者可能仅因抑郁发作而寻求帮助，而轻躁狂发作可能未被注意到。误诊可能发生，因为一些双相障碍症状与其他疾病的症状相似。例如，同时有精神病性症状的双相障碍患者可能被误诊为精神分裂症。为避免此类误诊，重要的是考虑过去数天和数周内障碍的病程，而不是仅关注当前症状。一些健康状况，如甲状腺疾病，可引起类似双相障碍的症状。某些处方药、娱乐性药物或非法药物的影响有时可模拟或加重情绪症状。如果双相障碍的细微迹象被遗漏，并且最初的抑郁发作仅用抗抑郁药治疗（不使用心境稳定剂），可能会触发躁狂发作或快速循环。

英文原文：
To diagnose bipolar disorder, a health care provider may complete a physical exam, order medical testing to rule out other illnesses, and refer the person for an evaluation by a mental health professional.
Bipolar disorder is diagnosed based on the severity, length, and frequency of an individual’s symptoms and experiences over their lifetime, and their family history.
Some people have bipolar disorder for years before it is diagnosed for several reasons. People with bipolar II disorder may seek help only for depressive episodes, and hypomanic episodes may go unnoticed.
Misdiagnosis may happen because some bipolar disorder symptoms are like those of other illnesses. For example, people with bipolar disorder who also have psychotic symptoms can be misdiagnosed with schizophrenia. To avoid such misdiagnosis, it is important to consider the course of the disorder over the past days and weeks, rather than focusing solely on the current symptoms. Some health conditions, such as thyroid disease, can cause symptoms like those of bipolar disorder. The effects of some prescribed, recreational, or illicit drugs can sometimes mimic or worsen mood symptoms.
If subtle signs of bipolar disorder are missed and an initial depressive episode is treated with antidepressant medication alone (without a mood stabilizer), a manic episode or rapid cycling may be triggered.

documents.content:
中文译文（自动翻译，待人工复核；以英文原文为准）：
许多双相障碍患者也患有其他精神障碍或疾病，例如焦虑障碍、注意缺陷/多动障碍（ADHD）、药物或酒精滥用，或进食障碍。有时，经历严重躁狂或抑郁发作的人也会出现精神病性症状，例如幻觉或妄想。精神病性症状往往与患者的极端心境相匹配。例如，在抑郁发作期间出现精神病性症状的人可能错误地相信自己经济上破产了，而在躁狂发作期间出现精神病性症状的人可能错误地相信自己出名或拥有特殊能力。观察疾病过程中的症状以及患者的家族史，有助于确定一个人是否同时患有双相障碍和另一种障碍。

英文原文：
Many people with bipolar disorder also have other mental disorders or conditions, such as anxiety disorders, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), misuse of drugs or alcohol, or eating disorders. Sometimes people who have severe manic or depressive episodes also have symptoms of psychosis, such as hallucinations or delusions. The psychotic symptoms tend to match the person’s extreme mood. For example, someone having psychotic symptoms during a depressive episode may falsely believe they are financially ruined, while someone having psychotic symptoms during a manic episode may falsely believe they are famous or have special powers.
Looking at symptoms over the course of the illness and the person’s family history can help determine whether a person has bipolar disorder along with another disorder.
